title: WRU posts pitch safety advice over hot, dry summer
description: The Welsh Rugby Union issues pitch safety advice for the new season after a record-breaking summer.
fullText:
The Welsh Rugby Union has issued pitch safety advice to community clubs for the new season after a record-breaking summer.

Wales recorded its hottest ever day on 24 June with temperatures soaring to 35.9C in Cardiff, while July was the driest since records began 190 years ago.

The weather has left rugby pitches across the country bone dry, with surfaces as hard as concrete.

With the obvious injury risks to players, the WRU has written to all community clubs with guidance on how to assess the conditions before next week's opening matches.

It also says clubs can reschedule fixtures without risking any sanction up until mid-September, while match officials can overrule decisions on safety grounds.

How are sports clubs coping with drought?

Drought leaves sports clubs 'praying for rain'

The WRU recommends stopping or delaying play against a series of check points.

They include uneven surfaces, where holes, cracks or sudden dips could cause a player to fall.

Clubs should also assess grass coverage, looking for bare and hard patches in contact zones (scrum, tackle areas, in-goal), along with surface hardness and shock absorbency.

"We are saying to our players and our clubs that it is very much 'game on' in Wales, but with the caveat that player safety and welfare must be an absolute priority when the decision is made at a local level about whether or not to play games," said WRU community director Geraint John.

"Games can go ahead where it is safe to do so but, equally, clubs and referees are entirely free to make the call to reschedule on safety grounds if there are any doubts whatsoever."

The current guidance lasts until 13 September, when an update will be issued.

title: What is the aim for Kompany, Kane and Bayern?
description: Bayern Munich start their latest title defence as overwhelming odds-on favourites to win the Bundesliga again - so what would constitute success?
fullText:
Bayern Munich start their latest title defence as overwhelming odds-on favourites to win the Bundesliga again - so what would consistute success this season?

The German side are as short as 1-7 odds with bookmakers after winning 13 of the past 14 titles - and are chasing a hat-trick of successes.

They host Stuttgart on Friday (19:30 BST) in a game you can watch live on BBC iPlayer and the BBC Sport website.

Vincent Kompany's side already have a win against rivals Borussia Dortmund under their belt after winning the German Super Cup 2-1 last weekend.

England captain Harry Kane will be looking to win his fourth Bundesliga Golden Boot in four seasons... and perhaps even more.

"The targets at Bayern are always set as high as possible, which means winning the Bundesliga, winning the cup, winning the Champions League and perhaps even winning every single match," said Kompany this summer.

BBC Sport has a look at what Bayern and Kane can hope for this season - and what is new.

Bundesliga: Bayern Munich v Stuttgart

Watch live on BBC iPlayer and the BBC Sport website and app.

Kane first Englishman to win Germany's player of the year award

Winning the Bundesliga title is more of an expectation than a cause for huge celebration at the Allianz Arena.

Since 2012 only once have they not been champions - when Bayer Leverkusen went unbeaten all season domestically in 2023-24.

In Kompany's two seasons at Bayern, since leaving Burnley, they have finished 13 and 16 points clear at the top.

Last season the German double winners were one of Europe's biggest entertainers, scoring 184 goals in all competitions.

They scored a record 122 goals in the Bundesliga and 43 in the Champions League, where they fell to Paris St-Germain 6-5 on aggregate in the semi-finals.

Since this era of dominance started with the 2012-13 Treble, including the Champions League, they have only won Europe's top trophy once since then - in 2020.

But German football writer Constantin Eckner says Kompany does "not necessarily" need to win it this season.

"Bayern's hierarchy have been very happy with him and the progress of the team," said Eckner.

"As long as they compete among the top four in Europe, they are content to have Kompany. He has brought back a notion of stability to Bayern's managerial post.

"Before that, it was quite the revolving door policy, as they had seven managers in eight years.

"The Belgian has been a revelation, and the feeling is he could become one of the best managers in the world.

"One could argue he is already among the best, though games like the one at Paris St-Germain have shown that he still has a few things to learn."

When Kane joined Bayern on a four-year deal in 2022 from Tottenham there was a feeling, certainly in England, that he might return home at the end of that deal.

Kane had never won a trophy during his time at Tottenham, or with England, so the pull of going to a team who win trophies nearly every year was strong.

But many also thought after bagging a few medals he would perhaps try to break the Premier League goalscoring record (sitting 47 behind Alan Shearer).

In fact he admitted as much last week, saying: "When I first left, for sure it was something I thought - I would definitely be coming back. That itch isn't there as much anymore."

The 33-year-old has loved his time at Bayern and says he is ready to begin discussions over extending that deal.

That love is very much mutual. Bayern honorary president Uli Hoeness has called Kane "the best signing we've ever made".

This is a club who have had some legendary goalscorers in Gerd Muller, Karl-Heinz Rummenigge and Robert Lewandowski.

Kane scored 61 goals in 51 club matches last season, the most a Bayern player has ever struck in one campaign.

That took his total to 146 goals - plus 33 assists - in 147 games for Bayern. He won the European Shoe in 2024 and 2026 and 'just' the regular Bundesliga Golden Boot in 2025.

He also scored all three goals in the German Cup final win over Stuttgart to complete the 2026 double.

"There are many fans who believe he could win the Ballon d'Or," said Eckner.

"Bayern are lobbying for it [and it is] also a sign towards the much younger Michael Olise that a move to Real Madrid wouldn't be necessary to win the Ballon d'Or.

"Kane has impressed with his very consistent and relentless goalscoring in the Bundesliga. He has essentially filled the shoes of Robert Lewandowksi, who put up similar numbers.

"Bayern rely heavily on Kane. They haven't signed a real back-up for him, nor a potential replacement. His contract runs out at the end of the season, but Bayern are sure he will extend for a few more years."

Were Kane to win the Ballon d'Or he would be only the second Englishman to win it since the 1970s and the first since Michael Owen in 2001.

"The Ballon d'Or is as big as it gets, from an individual point of view," he said.

"It's not in my hands. I've done what I can do in terms of putting in the performances. It's now down to votes and other people and the media - stuff I can't control - so we'll see what happens."

However last November Kane admitted: "I could score 100 goals this season, but if I don't win the Champions League or the World Cup, you're probably not going to win the Ballon d'Or."

He lost in the semi-final of both competitions.

Another one of Bayern's irreplaceable players is another Londoner in Olise, who represents France at international level.

The forward has scored 43 goals - including one in this season's Super Cup - with 46 assists in just over two years at the club.

Bayern have made little changes rather than a squad overhaul this summer, not surprising after two good seasons.

They have recruited Germany left-back Nathaniel Brown from Eintracht Frankfurt for a fee thought to be about £47m.

The 23-year-old can also play on the wing - and even featured in the number 10 role in the Super Cup, where he scored on his debut.

The other big signing is Morocco international Ismael Saibari from PSV for a reported £43m.

Like Brown, the 27-year-old is versatile and can play in midfield or anywhere up front. He scored three times at the World Cup.

The highest profile exits have been Germany midfielder Leon Goretzka, 31, and versatile Portuguese wideman Raphael Guerreiro, 32.

Both have left as free agents at the end of their contracts.

Senegal striker Nicolas Jackson returned to Chelsea at the end of his season-long loan.

Bayern will also have to manage the situation with Jamal Musiala this season.

The 23-year-old attacking midfielder says he is being treated for a "neurological dysfunction" after collapsing during two friendlies this summer.

He added they were "temporary, brief, but easily treatable absence seizures".

"I'm receiving excellent medical treatment and am very optimistic," he continued.

"FC Bayern and my family and friends are always by my side and supporting me on this journey."

title: Former QPR player Buzsaky confirms he is safe
description: Former QPR midfielder Akos Buzsaky posts a message on social media to confirm he is safe after being reported missing.
fullText:
Former QPR midfielder Akos Buzsaky has posted a message on social media to confirm he is safe after being reported missing.

On Wednesday, reports emerged from his native Hungary that Buzsaky had been missing for more than a week, and that police were looking for him.

However, Buzsaky posted on Facebook on Friday, external to reassure people that he was OK and thanked them for their concern about his welfare.

In the message, which QPR posted on X,, external former Hungary midfielder Buzsaky said: "Unfortunately, in the last few months, there have been serious changes in my life that have tested me.

"There came a moment when I felt I had to break away from these daily routines."

He went on to say that his mother had contacted the police after a "misunderstanding".

Buzsaky added: "A soon as I learned about the situation, I stopped my retreat and informed the authorities.

"Thank you very much for all the concern and thoughts you have shown me.

"I wish everyone a nice day, and it felt really good to receive so much love!"

The 44-year-old spent five seasons at Loftus Road after joining the London side on loan in 2007.

He also played for Plymouth, Portsmouth, and Barnsley during his time in the UK, scoring a total of 33 goals in 243 appearances.

title: Artist defends 'unfinished' O'Sullivan mural
description: The mural on a snooker club wall has gone viral - but artist says "touch-ups" are still needed.
fullText:
A Sheffield street artist has defended his mural of snooker player Ronnie O'Sullivan after the design received criticism - saying that the project is "unfinished".

Chris Ashmore was commissioned to produce the artwork featuring seven-time world champion O'Sullivan for the back wall of the Spot On Snooker Club on Langsett Road.

Although many residents said they liked the mural, others described it as "zombie-like", "shocking" and O'Sullivan's face as "skeletal".

Ashmore said he was surprised by the viral response online, but confirmed that he had only completed two weeks out of the five assigned to the job, and "touch-ups" were still needed.

The local artist said part of the problem was that he had been working from a scaffolding platform which obstructed his view, meaning he didn't get the "full perspective".

"I usually use a scissor lift, where you can stand back and see things as a whole, but I couldn't use it as the land is too uneven," he explained.

"When the scaffolding came down, I came away and boom - it's gone viral.

"I saw people saying it looks like Michael Jackson or a zombie. I've got thick skin, I'll be OK, but it didn't feel fair."

People living near the snooker and pool club had mixed feelings about the mural.

Gillian Jones said she liked it and it "brightened her day".

Glen Bridock said he was "a fan of the Rocket" and thought the design looked "brilliant".

Frank Short conceded that "the artwork is ok but the eyes are all wrong. It looks like he's taken something".

Shaun Spalding described the art as "shocking"

"His eyes are all wrong, his teeth are wrong, it just don't look like Ronnie. It looks like somebody who's got a skeletal face."

Dan Kirkland, the manager of Spot On, also defended Ashmore's work.

He said: "Yes, we've seen what you've seen. There are parts of the face that need tweaking, particularly around the eye and mouth.

"Some relatively small changes will make a huge difference, so we'll arrange whatever access Chris needs.

"What has upset us is seeing some of the reactions becoming personal towards Chris.

"People are absolutely entitled to like or dislike a mural. But having an opinion about a piece of artwork is one thing. Slagging off the person who created it is another."

Ashmore, who has completed numerous murals for businesses, said he had always intended to hire a cherry picker to finish the job, but would not be pressured into "rushing" it.

"It's not finished, there's bits of skin tone to do and I'll finish it off as and when I can.

"I'm not just going to rush it in three days because people have complained on social media. I want to do it properly in my own time."

title: Celtic & Rangers to play Scottish Cup ties behind closed doors after fan disorder
description: Celtic and Rangers are ordered to play their next home Scottish Cup ties behind closed doors after fan disorder last season.
fullText:
Celtic and Rangers have both been ordered to play their next home Scottish Cup matches behind closed doors after last season's quarter-final was marred by fan disorder.

Both clubs will also have to pay £100,000 to the team they are drawn against in that fixture.

The two clubs could also face a second home match without fans if there is a further incident of either side's supporters engaging in "unacceptable conduct" in a Scottish Cup fixture.

Celtic progressed to last season's semi-finals by beating Rangers on penalties at Ibrox, after which fans of both teams spilled on to the pitch.

The sanctions are likely to come into force when both sides enter this season's Scottish Cup in January.

Celtic said: "We are shocked by this disproportionate punishment for a relatively small incursion by Celtic supporters at a moment of emotion and celebration.

"Our club has never defended supporters entering the field of play and we have repeatedly taken action when it occurs.

"However, we understand the part emotion plays in football and would have expected the context and distinction in behaviours to have been taken into account by the panel.

"Another important distinction is that, on this occasion, Celtic were not the home club, responsible for stadium safety arrangements.

"We will study the panel's report and reasoning when it is available and will thereafter consider our next steps."

Three more arrests after Old Firm fan disorder

The sanctions relate to the scenes in March after Celtic's penalty shootout victory, when supporters threw fireworks and other missiles, police officers were injured and a number of arrests were made.

Both clubs gave evidence to an independent judicial panel after being charged under the Scottish FA's disciplinary rule 37, which covers unacceptable conduct at matches.

An independent review published last month concluded the incident came within a "very small margin" of becoming a violent mass confrontation.

The report, led by Mark Blackbourne, identified failings by both clubs and criticised the Scottish FA for not taking a tougher approach to crowd disorder.

In the recent past, the SFA and SPFL have handed down fines and, on occasion, reduced ticket allocations for issues such as the use of pyrotechnics, but the severity of this sanction signals a shift in approach.

The SFA has not escaped its share of the criticism by the independent review, but the panel's report provided the governing body with the cover it needed to get tougher on an ever-growing problem.

And while it comes as no surprise to see the clubs defending their positions, when the dust settles, the SFA will hope that these sanctions will send out a clear message that unacceptable conduct will no longer be tolerated.

title: Callaway drops golf brand over sexist video row
description: Golf club manufacturer Callaway ends its partnership with content creator Good Good with immediate effect and donates $1m to women's charity after promoting advert that shows a woman being pushed over.
fullText:
Golf club manufacturer Callaway has ended its partnership with content creator Good Good with immediate effect following backlash over a video which showed a woman being pushed to the ground after reaching for a club.

American golf brand Good Good has one of the most popular sport YouTube channels with 2.13m subscribers and had created and published the advert for Callaway last week.

But the video drew widespread criticism and was accused of making light of violence against women, and both companies removed the advert and issued apologies.

Good Good, who Callaway has worked with since 2023, has also stepped away from its sponsorship of a PGA Tour event in Austin, Texas in November.

On Thursday, Callaway, in a statement on X,, external conceded its content review process "was not comprehensive enough", adding that it had "listened and reflected deeply on the hurt and disappointment caused by the video we reposted".

The manufacturer said it was also donating $1m (£735,725) to organisations working to prevent violence against women and support victims.

"We heard from individuals who shared personal experiences related to violence against women, and their stories were powerful reminders that this issue touches the lives of far too many people," Callaway's statement read.

"Unequivocally, violence against women is unacceptable and should never be trivialised, normalised, or used as entertainment."

Callaway said they have taken "appropriate internal corrective actions" to help ensure this does not happen again.

The advert showed Good Good co-founder Garrett Clark rushing over to Alexis Miestowski - a professional golfer and regular content creator for Good Good - and pushing her to the ground before shouting: "Do not touch my new driver."

The brand, which has become one of the largest content creators in golf, launched its YouTube channel 2020.

Regular clips include men and women competing in various golf challenges, while Good Good also creates made-for-TV shows as well as adverts for golf clothing and other merchandise.

After pulling out as sponsors of the PGA Tour tournament, Good Good chief executive officer Matt Kendrick said they "remain committed to earning back" the tour's trust.

"We recognise that we have work to do as an organisation, and our focus right now is on our team, our culture and ensuring we learn from this situation." Kendrick added in a statement.

title: Sunderland and Bournemouth draw AC Milan in Europa League
description: Sunderland will mark their first European campaign since 1973 with a trip to the San Siro after drawing AC Milan in the Europa League league phase.
fullText:
Sunderland will mark their first European campaign since 1973 with a trip to the San Siro after drawing AC Milan in the Europa League.

The Black Cats, who finished seventh in the Premier League last season, will face the seven-time European champions in one of their eight league-phase matches.

One of their four away matches will come against European debutants Torreense.

The second-tier side earned qualification for the Europa League by inflicting a shock defeat on Sporting CP to win the Portuguese Cup final in May.

But as their 2,500-capacity home stadium in Torres Vedras does not meet Uefa's requirements, they will play their home matches 193 miles away at the Estadio Algarve in Faro.

Bournemouth have also been handed a tie against AC Milan, although theirs will be on home soil.

The Cherries, who have qualified for European football for the first time, will also face Real Sociedad among their eight games.

Last season's Conference League winners Crystal Palace have been handed arguably the toughest draw out of the three Premier League teams, with Pierre Sage's side set up for meetings with Lyon, Real Sociedad and Besiktas.

It will be the first time Palace have competed in the Europa League, having been demoted from the competition last July for breaching multi-club ownership rules.

Scottish Premiership champions Celtic, who fell into the Europa League after surrendering a four-goal lead against LASK in the Champions League play-off tie earlier this week, will take on Marseille, Benfica and Besiktas.

In the Conference League, Brighton's draw includes fixtures against AS Monaco and Spanish side Getafe.

Hearts have also been drawn against Monaco and will also face a trip to Mohamed Salah's Trabzonspor.

The Europa League final will take place in Frankfurt on 26 May, with the Conference League equivalent taking place six days later in Istanbul.

Sunderland: AZ Alkmaar (home), AC Milan (away), GNK Dinamo (home), Anderlecht (away), Jagiellonia (home), Lech Poznan (away), Levski Sofia (home), Torreense (away)

Bournemouth: AC Milan (home), Real Sociedad (away), Viktoria Plzen (home), Sparta Praha (away), Sturm Graz (home), Celta Vigo (away), Hapoel Be'er Sheva (home), Lillestrom (away)

Crystal Palace: Real Sociedad (home), Lyon (away), Sparta Praha (home), Salzburg (away), Lech Poznan (home), Jagiellonia (away), Hoffenheim (home), Besiktas (away).

Celtic: Marseille (home), Benfica (away), Ferencvaros (home), Union SG (away), Celta Vigo (home), Omonia (away), Besiktas (home), Torreense (away)

Brighton: Monaco (home), Panathinaikos (away), Craiova (home), Getafe (away), Kauno Zalgiris (home), Jablonec (away).

Hearts: Monaco (home), Pafos (away), Borac (home), Trabzonspor (away), Nordsjaelland (home), Thun (away)

In the Europa League, each of the 36 teams will play eight different teams, four at home and four away, in the league phase.

The teams who finish in the top eight will automatically qualify for the round of 16, while those who finish between ninth and 24th will face off in a two-legged knockout tie in the play-off round.

Teams who finish 25th and below will be eliminated from the competition and will not be able to drop into any other European competitions.

In the Conference League, the format of the league phase has the 36 teams playing six games, three at home and three away.

And like the Europa League, the top eight progress to the last 16, while teams finishing between ninth and 24th enter the play-offs.

In the Europa League last season, Aston Villa went on to win the title.

In the Conference League, Crystal Palace had to overcome Bosnian side Zrinjski Mostar in the play-off round after finishing 10th in the league phase.

The Eagles then beat AEK Larnaca, Fiorentina and Shakhtar Donetsk in the knockout rounds before defeating Rayo Vallecano in the final in Leipzig to win their first European trophy.

title: Leknessund seals first Grand Tour stage win
description: Norway's Andreas Leknessund takes an emotional first Grand Tour stage win as he climbs to victory on stage seven of the Vuelta a Espana.
fullText:
Norway's Andreas Leknessund secured an emotional first Grand Tour stage win as he led home a Norwegian one-two on stage seven of the Vuelta a Espana.

The 27-year-old was part of the break from the start of the stage and after 137 kilometres he left behind his remaining companions on the last climb to ride the final seven kilometres solo, winning by 34 seconds from fellow Norwegian and Uno-X Mobility team-mate Tobias Halland Johannessen, with Wout van Aert finishing third.

"It really hurt today," said Lenessund. "I didn't expect it to be this emotional."

A Norwegian one-two was fitting given Norway's King Harald V died on Friday, with both riders sporting black armbands in his memory.

World champion Tadej Pogacar, who is looking to complete a full set of Grand Tour victories, finished 19th - four minutes and 23 seconds behind the winner - but extended his lead in the general classification by a further 16 seconds after pulling clear of his main rivals with a few kilometres to go.

Britain's Oscar Onley lost further time to the red jersey but climbed to sixth in GC and took a firm grip on the young rider's classification, now leading the battle for the white jersey by nearly four minutes.

title: Ruiz named Brighton boss after shock Vidosic exit
description: Brighton have confirmed the appointment of Arturo Ruiz as their new women's head coach following the shock departure of Dario Vidosic.
fullText:
Brighton have confirmed the appointment of Arturo Ruiz as their new women's head coach following the shock departure of Dario Vidosic.

Ruiz, 29, has signed a contract until 2029 and will join the Women's Super League (WSL) club once his work permit is finalised.

His appointment comes hours after it was confirmed Australia Vidosic was stepping down from his role as manager just a week before the start of the season.

Brighton said Vidosic has left "to pursue a new opportunity", and it is believed a move to the United States is on the cards, with sources saying National Women's Soccer League side Angel City are the most likely destination.

Ruiz joins Brighton from Real Sociedad, where he took over as head coach in July 2025.

He held his first managerial position at Atletico Madrid and guided them to a third-place finish in Liga F, securing Women's Champions League qualification.

The Spaniard later joined Granada CF before becoming Real Sociedad's head coach, again finishing third in the league.

"We are delighted to welcome Arturo to the club," said Zoe Johnson, Brighton's women's and girls' managing director.

"During our recruitment process, he quickly stood out. He has a proven track record of developing teams and individuals.

"We have confidence in his ability to drive this team forward and he will have our full support as we make our final preparations for the start of the new WSL season."

Find interviews and extra content on the BBC Women's Football Weekly feed

I missed being valued as a footballer - Walti

Despite the swift appointment, Vidosic's departure is still a major blow for Brighton.

The Australian joined from Melbourne City in 2024 and signed a three-year deal as Brighton sought to close in on the WSL's top four.

In his first season in charge, Vidosic led them to a fifth-place finish - their best in the WSL - and they recorded memorable wins over Arsenal and Manchester City in 2025-26.

Most notably, they reached the Women's FA Cup final for the first time in the club's history in May.

"I have loved my time at Albion and am proud of what we have achieved together," Vidosic said.

"Leaving has been a difficult decision but I believe it is the right time for me and my family to begin a new chapter.

"I would like to thank the players, staff and supporters for their support throughout my time at the club and wish everyone associated with Albion every success."

With a week to go before the new season, Brighton were being tipped as one of the clubs capable of challenging WSL big hitters Arsenal, Chelsea, Manchester City and Manchester United for a top-four place.

They kick off their WSL season at home to Arsenal on Sunday, 6 September (12:00 BST).

Brighton have taken big strides in recent seasons and the club have invested in the playing squad, so they will be gutted to lose Vidosic.

He was brought in as a relatively unknown coach in Europe having started his post-playing career in Australia.

A two-year spell at Melbourne City showed his potential and since joining Brighton, Vidosic has quickly become one of the most respected coaches in England.

His style of play has been exciting and creative, though it has meant Brighton have lacked consistency at times.

However, they showed during his two seasons in charge that they were capable of taking on the WSL's giants and were rewarded with an FA Cup final last year.

All signs pointed to a positive future as the club announced in April its plans for Europe's first purpose-built women's stadium, costing in the region of £80m.

They had attracted big-name players such as England's Euro 2022 winner Fran Kirby, and this summer they signed Switzerland captain Lia Walti.

But the timing of Vidosic's exit is a massive blow and while the plan was to kick on and close in on a top four spot, they must now undergo a managerial transition.

From Vidosic's perspective, the NWSL remains one of the world's best leagues and he is likely to have more of a say in recruitment and the club's overall project.

New signings joined Brighton to play under Vidosic and his style of football, so will the club's recruitment suit Ruiz?

The Spaniard has made a name for himself in his home country and has a clear style - but he only has days before the WSL season kicks off.

It means Brighton are likely to be on the back foot at the start of a campaign in which they hoped to build momentum.

title: Rangers count consequences of 'devoid of quality' European failure
description: A bruising loss in the Czech Republic gives Rangers pause on various fronts as European football eludes Derek McInnes.
fullText:
After Jablonec's Jan Chramosta converted from the penalty spot to confirm Rangers' European exit on Thursday, the immediate reaction from the away end was one of understandable anger.

Manager Derek McInnes said he was "embarrassed" and "disappointed" by both the performance and the result as his difficult start at Ibrox continued.

Just one shot on target in 120 minutes against a team they were firm favourites to beat, multiples changes of shape and a multitude of signings failing to have an impact.

But what exactly are the consequences of Rangers missing out on European football this season, both on and off the pitch?

One of the main benefits of playing European competitions is the financial boost it provides.

Rangers finishing third in the Scottish Premiership last season meant they did not have the opportunity to qualify for the Champions League and they were knocked out of Europa League qualifying by Polish side Jagiellonia Bialystok in a further blow.

However, they still had the chance to reach the Conference League - admittedly, the least prestigious and least lucrative of Uefa's three club competitions.

Teams that qualify for the league phase of the Conference League receive about £2.72m, with about £343,000 more for every win at that stage. There is a further £114,000 for a league-phase draw.

There are then exponential rewards for reaching the knockout stages and each win from there on.

Last season's Conference League winners Crystal Palace received at least £15m from the competition, plus the bonus of qualifying for this season's Europa League.

There is also the knock-on effect of fewer matchdays and therefore fewer tickets sold, as well as hospitality and corporate packages.

It remains to be seen if Rangers' summer spending spree will be curtailed by defeat in the Czech Republic.

The Ibrox outfit continue to be linked with a big-money move for Portland Timbers striker Kevin Kelsy, as they try to replace the injured Youssef Chermiti up front.

Another winger also appears to be a priority, with talks reportedly ongoing with Brighton for Amario Cozier-Duberry.

Daisuke Yokota and Kim Min-su have already arrived to join wide players Ross McCausland, Findlay Curtis and Djeidi Gassama.

Might influential midfielder Nicolas Raskin - who did not travel to Jablonec - be sold to fund more new players?

What is clear, Rangers in their current guise do not look capable of challenging for silverware this term.

"When you look at the performance, it is nowhere near good enough, but not a result I didn't expect," former Hibernian and Celtic midfielder Scott Allan said on the BBC's Scottish Football Podcast.

"He literally said himself the team doesn't know what it is. And ultimately that falls on Derek McInnes and what they're doing on the training pitch.

"He talked about elite preparation - the performance was anything but that. If we're totally honest, they're devoid of quality.

"Rangers weren't playing against a top side. That's a game, with what Rangers have spent, they should be coming through quite comfortably."

Podcast: From European agony to weekend Premiership pressure

One saving grace might be fewer games helping sharpen Rangers' focus in domestic competitions.

Title favourites Celtic will have to navigate at least eight matches in the Europa League, while Hearts - who also finished above Rangers last season - succeeded where Rangers failed and reached the Conference League proper, where they have at least six games.

It's a bleak picture for Scotland and its Uefa coefficient.

After being ranked as high as ninth between 2021 and 2023, at the end of last season Scotland had plummeted to 18th.

This is important because it determines how many places a league gets in Europe each season - and in which competitions.

For instance, last season's placings in the Scottish Premiership earned five places in Europe. For this season going into next, it's down to four.

Scotland is now down to one place in the Champions League, starting in the early rounds.

To get places back, Scotland needs to get back into the top 15. But this week's disastrous results mean there's no chance of that.

Celtic being knocked out of the Champions League and going into the Europa League did not really matter, as it's easier to get results in the secondary competition.

But three of the other teams being knocked out of Europe means there's only a small chance of climbing up the coefficient table.

Historically, Scotland has relied upon the Old Firm for its European results. So Rangers being eliminated is a huge blow.

Now, Hearts will have to step up and make it deep into the Conference League, results in which are worth far fewer coefficient points.

Scotland has already dropped to 19th in the live standings but would need to drop to 34th for the current allocation to be impacted. That cannot happen.

But the gap to 15th is considerable and Scotland would need their best ever season to bridge it.

The good news is, at the end of this season, the 2022-23 season drops off the five-year calculation. And that was one of Scotland's worst seasons.

But if teams continue to fail in the qualifying rounds, Scotland will struggle to reclaim places in Europe.

title: I'd hate to finish career like this - O'Sullivan
description: Ronnie O'Sullivan says he does not "want to throw in the towel just yet" after losing 6-3 to Chang Bingyu in the semi-finals of the Wuhan Open.
fullText:
Ronnie O'Sullivan says he does not "want to throw in the towel just yet" after being beaten 6-3 by Chang Bingyu in the semi-finals of the Wuhan Open on Friday.

The seven-time world champion fought back against China Open winner Mark Selby in the quarter-finals on Thursday to seal a 5-3 victory, but he has spoken candidly at this week's ranking event about his struggles.

O'Sullivan has taken steps to prioritise his mental health in recent years, withdrawing from tournaments and discussing his battles with depression and anxiety.

"The disease came back big time today," said the 50-year-old Englishman. "If I'm honest I don't think I will ever get over it."

Artist defends 'unfinished' Ronnie O'Sullivan mural

O'Sullivan, who has not won a ranking event for more than two years, added: "I will see out the next 18 months and see how we go. I don't want to throw the towel in just yet. I've committed to playing until then.

"I want to give myself a chance. I'd hate to finish my career on performances like that."

O'Sullivan lost the opening two frames against Chang but pulled himself back into the match to head into the mid-session break level at 2-2.

When play resumed, China's Chang took control, winning two frames in a row to lead 4-2.

O'Sullivan pulled one back but breaks of 69 and 48 in the following frames booked Chang a place in Saturday's final - and his first win against 'The Rocket'.

"Every time I play against Ronnie, it's a pleasure," said 24-year-old Chang.

"He probably wasn't in the best form today, and I managed to take some of the opportunities that came my way."

Chang will face new world number one Zhao Xintong in the final after he dashed Xiao Guodong's hopes of winning in Wuhan for the third successive year.

Zhao, who won the world title in 2025, took the opening two frames before being pegged back to 2-2.

However, he made two half-centuries as he reeled off the next four frames and constructed a superb break of 124 to round off his 6-2 victory.

title: Hrgovic slaps Itauma after being pushed off stage at weigh-in
description: British heavyweight Moses Itauma pushes Filip Hrgovic off the stage before the Croat slaps him as chaos erupts at the weigh-in for Saturday's world-title bout.
fullText:
British heavyweight Moses Itauma pushed Filip Hrgovic off the stage before the Croat slapped him as chaos erupted at the weigh-in for Saturday's world-title bout.

The pair will fight for the vacant IBF heavyweight title at London's O2 Arena, with Itauma bidding to become the second-youngest heavyweight champion in history.

The 21-year-old had refused to engage with Hrgovic's attempts to rile him during fight week but was in a fierce mood as the pair exchanged expletives during a charged face-off.

As Hrgovic turned to pose for photographs, Itauma shoved him in the back, sending the 34-year-old off the stage.

Hrgovic climbed back up, reached through security and slapped the Chatham fighter in the face before members of both teams became involved as security separated them.

"He pushed me first so I just gave it back. He started it," Hrgovic said, before breaking off from the interview to stare down Itauma.

Will fast-tracked Itauma become world champion at 21?

I'll send Itauma back to high school - Hrgovic

Itauma 'million times better' than Fury and Joshua - Hamed

Earlier in the week, Itauma said Hrgovic - who has repeatedly labelled him a "kid" - was beginning to get under his skin.

"I don't know, I just lost it a little bit. I had a little itch and I had to scratch it," Itauma said.

Before the fracas, an in-shape Hrgovic had weighed in at his lightest in seven years - 16st 12lb (107kg), 12 pounds lighter than for his victory over Dave Allen in May.

Itauma, who would also become the second-youngest world champion from Britain if he wins, weighed 17st 4lb (110kg), the same as for his victory over Jermaine Franklin in March.

Friday's ceremonial weigh-in took place at London's Spitalfields Market, with the official weigh-in held behind closed doors earlier in the day.

Several hundred people gathered around the food stalls and coffee kiosks for the event, with Itauma walking through the crowd to loud cheers.

He was smiling as he made his way through the market, where some had come specifically for the weigh-in while others were simply passing through and stopped to see what the fuss was about.

Itauma has the unbeaten record, knockout power and reputation as one of boxing's brightest young talents, but is still building his profile outside the sport.

Sometimes, though, it is what happens outside the ring that gets people talking.

The incident did not appear premeditated, with Itauma looking irritated by what Hrgovic was saying before the shove.

"He wants to stamp his authority and I think that's what he was doing there - stamping his authority before he gets in the ring," promoter Frank Warren said.

"He's showing he's not fazed by what Filip brings with his experience and sterling amateur background. He's up for this, alight and on fire."

title: Division, drama and power - what next for Infantino and Uefa?
description: Explosive court documents reveal the growing bitterness of Uefa's feud with Fifa president Gianni Infantino, Dan Roan reports.
fullText:
"On information and belief, Infantino's actions described herein rise to the level of criminal mismanagement."

"A stunning dereliction of duty."

"A fraudulently off-market price promoted by Infantino for his own benefit."

Just some of the blistering language used by Uefa's lawyers in legal papers lodged in the United States over Fifa president Gianni Infantino's now-shelved plan to sell off stakes in competitions to private investors.

A scheme, Uefa claims, that awarded the World Cup an "absurdly low enterprise value... that was neither the product of an open, competitive auction, nor tested by any independent valuer". All part of "a transaction that inflicted direct and concrete injury... to the detriment of Fifa as well as its 211 members", and was conducted under "a veil of secrecy".

The court documents, which reference Infantino's "cronies" and "co-conspirators", and include a chapter on "the enduring history of corruption among Fifa officials", request access to evidence and documents in the US for use in potential litigation in Switzerland against Infantino.

More than a month since the Fifa Forward Enterprise plan (FFE) was revealed, before collapsing days later, this increasingly acrimonious civil war shows little sign of ending.

Since then, we have seen the strongest public pressure from those opposed to Infantino with a series of cutting statements, including from former players, politicians, and fan groups.

And there was even the leaking of claims - labelled "categorically untrue" by Infantino - that his alleged lover was given a severance payment over the affair while he was at Uefa.

Now we have the threat of legal proceedings.

It is ironic that Infantino has enjoyed arguably his best week since this saga began.

On Thursday, he received the qualified backing of the powerful Saudi Arabian Football Federation, which said that "at this time [it] supports the continued efforts of Gianni Infantino to restore unity".

Despite defying calls from three confederations and various other stakeholders to stand down, Uefa's decision to drop its threat of boycotting Fifa competitions after receiving assurances there would be no repeat of the FFE scheme was seen as another victory for him.

But Uefa then raised the stakes. News that it was preparing criminal legal proceedings was viewed as a dramatic escalation, and evidence that it was not backing down in its determination to oust Infantino.

Although Infantino defended FFE as a means of unlocking the commercial potential of Fifa, before later apologising for "errors", neither he nor Fifa have responded to this latest twist, with officials insisting they are focused on delivering the U20 Women's World Cup, starting next week in Poland.

Infantino, meanwhile, fresh from trips to the Dominican Republic and Paris last weekend, posted video of a "wonderful" visit to Vietnam, the latest stop on what is increasingly resembling a world tour aimed at shoring up support.

Given that Uefa first warned of potential legal action almost a month ago, when it instructed Fifa to retain any "relevant materials" related to the plan, Infantino may well have anticipated Uefa's move, so how might he feel now?

Much may depend on whether US courts side with Uefa over its requests for disclosure of evidence related to the FFE plan. In documents seen by BBC Sport, it is seeking information from three parties; Fifa, Thrive Capital - the venture capital firm earmarked as the lead investor in FFE along with its founder Josh Kushner, and former Formula 1 chief Greg Maffei, who is described as "the key commercial adviser" on the proposed deal.

While the filings state that neither Kushner or Maffei are anticipated defendants in any proceedings, in the case of Kushner for instance, Uefa's lawyers say they are seeking subpoenas for "the production of documents and communications and for deposition testimony".

Although Kushner, who is the brother of US president Donald Trump's son-in-law, is yet to comment, some legal experts believe he could successfully challenge and block such a subpoena request by arguing that the details of the deal need to remain confidential to protect his business interests and future investments. Kushner has recently agreed a deal to buy basketball's Los Angeles Lakers for a record £9.3bn.

It is unclear how long this process could take, or whether Uefa will secure the evidence it needs to support its claim that the World Cup was deliberately undervalued at about £15bn. Nor is it clear whether it will ultimately follow through on its threat to lodge a criminal complaint in Switzerland.

How confident Uefa would be of criminal charges being brought is also highly uncertain. In 2002, in echoes of the current disunity, several Fifa executive committee members filed a criminal complaint against former president Sepp Blatter with a Zurich court, external. The public prosecutor took no action, while Blatter denied wrongdoing. Last year, a long-running attempt by the Swiss Attorney General's Office to prosecute Blatter and former Uefa president Michel Platini ended with both men being fully cleared of corruption charges.

"What Uefa have to show is that they have an arguable case for criminal proceedings to be brought against Infantino," says leading sports lawyer Nick de Marco KC.

"If they can show that…then they ought to be given disclosure of a lot of the documents."

When asked what he thought the chances were of the case eventually going to trial, De Marco said: "We're a long way off from that - the first stage is this disclosure application.

"My own view is that the likelihood of success in that, which is very important, is high, but then it's a question for the Swiss prosecutor, looking at that disclosure, to decide whether there is a case [and] that will take some time...but I think what we will likely see is disclosure of very interesting documents and more light shone onto this plan."

Perhaps aware of the challenges its legal action could face, Uefa has in the meantime pledged to "secure fundamental reform, restore proper limits on presidential authority and ensure that Fifa is once again governed as an institution - not around one individual", while demanding "a genuinely independent external review of FFE".

Given the support he retains in South America, Africa and parts of Asia, and how he has survived everything Uefa has thrown at him in recent weeks, many still expect Infantino to remain in power and seek re-election for a fourth term in the spring. Uefa has warned that, should he do so, it will "join forces with its partner confederations to ensure that member associations are offered a credible alternative - one committed to integrity, accountability, development and genuine institutional change".

But how likely is it that a unifying challenger will emerge? And how can the game avoid a repeat of such a crisis in future?

"We have some clarity over the changes that are needed to modernise football governance and to make it run in a way that is accountable to its most important stakeholders," Uefa vice-president Laura McAllister told BBC Sport in Monaco.

"I think there are lots of credible candidates out there, but it has to be a candidate that can unite that standpoint and somebody who has the credentials and the credibility and the buy-in to really champion that agenda.

"We need to make the governance itself rooted on the principles that are so important like transparency and independence and critical challenge and due diligence.

"We knew this wouldn't be a simple process and we knew that change wouldn't happen overnight."

In October, Infantino will finally come face-to-face with some of his opponents at what could be a highly charged first Fifa Council meeting since the rebellion over FFE. The following month, presidential candidates must be nominated. Then, in March, an election is scheduled that, if contested by Infantino, could prove pivotal to the future direction of football.

Until then, the division and rancour that has engulfed the world's game in this remarkable drama of intrigue and power looks set to continue.

And right now, reunification seems hard to imagine.

title: Departing Watkins apologised for refusing to play - Emery
description: Ollie Watkins is leaving Aston Villa as their record Premier League goalscorer.
fullText:
Manager Unai Emery said Ollie Watkins apologised for refusing to play for Aston Villa on Sunday as he paid an emotional tribute to the departing striker.

The 30-year-old is expected in Saudi Arabia on Friday to complete a £51m move to Al-Hilal, with Villa poised to finalise the signing of Chelsea's Nicolas Jackson for £65m as his replacement.

Emery praised the England forward's behaviour during his Villa career and said he and the squad had accepted Watkins' apology for making himself unavailable against Brighton.

Watkins is Villa's record Premier League scorer with 91 goals, part an overall tally of 108 in all competitions since signing from Brentford for £28m in 2020.

"He told us after the Brighton match he was sorry and that he had made a mistake. He was wrong, but we accepted it. The players as well," said Emery.

"His commitment and his behaviour was fantastic. He's a fantastic guy - a fantastic guy even more than a player. I told him 'bye' with a huge hug and with small tears.

"But now it's a new chapter here with Nicolas Jackson."

Villa have agreed a deal for Jackson and are trying to ensure the Senegal striker is registered for Monday's visit of Arsenal.

Watkins is the latest experienced player to leave Villa this summer and Emery urged supporters to back the club's strategy despite the loss of several key figures in their successful 2025-26 season.

"We took decisions because it's good for the club," Emery said.

"Of course, we don't want to be a club that sells players, but the responsibility is there. It's crazy [money for someone] 30 years old and £50m for Ezri Konsa [who is 28].

"How we developed in the last year with some players and how we can sell some players now is completely the right decision.

"We have to rebuild the team as fast as possible. [Fans] have to accept our way and why we are taking some decisions."

As part of the rebuild, Leon Goretzka completed his move on a free transfer to Villa on Thursday after leaving Bayern Munich at the end of last season.

The midfielder won seven Bundesliga titles and the Champions League with Bayern.

"He is a winner. He is a very competitive player - a good player to add into our squad," said Emery.

"He is versatile and arrives fit and training well. Hopefully on Monday he can be on the field."

title: How Many Fascist Cronies Can One Republican Have?
description: Jeet...
fullText:
Georgia Senate candidate Mike Collins seems determined to answer that question.

Not for the first time, Republican Georgia congressman and Senate nominee Mike Collins is having to fend off questions about a former staffer’s florid public embrace of racism. On Thursday, The Washington Post reported that “a former staffer for Representative Mike Collins (R-Georgia) shared images in June and July on his X account of a swastika and one that depicts himself in Ku Klux Klan robes.”

The former staffer in question is 24-year-old Mike Parra, who worked as an intern for Collins as well as a contractor for a pro-Collins leadership PAC. Parra says he was merely being “satirical,” and that he is not really a white supremacist. But he has also described himself as a “twink fascist,” used anti-Black slurs, and said he thinks “the white race contributes more to the world,” which most people would recognize as the core belief of white supremacists.

Since Parra no longer works for Collins, his racist posts might seem a minor matter. But this is not the first such scandal involving Collins and his staff—not by a long shot.

As The Washington Post sums up:

A number of people in Collins’s orbit have been accused of having ties to white nationalists or of making racist or antisemitic comments, and the congressman’s own social media presence has also drawn scrutiny….

Collins, a trucking executive, has faced scrutiny over his own social media feed, where he has shared posts that were called racist and antisemitic, allegations he has denied….

In July, Collins replaced his…chief of staff Kip Talley after Slate reported on his participation in a group chat that included Nick Fuentes and Richard Spencer, both of whom are white supremacists and antisemites….

CNN reported in July that Collins’s son-in-law, David Alan Scheer II, has shared Nazi imagery online.…

In May, another Collins ex-staffer, William Paul, confronted Rep. Mike Lawler (R-New York) at a bar, hurling antisemitic insults at him…

Having one racist crony may be regarded as a misfortune. Having several should make even the most naïve investigator suspicious.

Aside from these incidents of racism and antisemitism from various confederates, Collins also fired another staffer, Brandon Phillips, for a vile post mocking the attempted suicide of the wife of a rival political consultant. The viciousness of that post shares an affinity with the racist trolling that Collins and his associates have often indulged in.

It’s a mistake to see this nastiness and bigotry as having no wider importance beyond the individuals concerned. Rather, they reflect a political fact that extends beyond Collins: Over the past 10 years, racist invective has become one of the main ways that the GOP activates its base and courts younger voters. It was not by chance that figures like Parra and Phillips worked for Collins. Rather, their passion for outré violations of common decency were what made them desirable employees—until they went too far and had to be disavowed.

In 2017, in the wake of the infamous Unite the Right march in Charlottesville, Virginia, the journalist Alex Pareene wrote a remarkably prophetic essay for Splinter arguing that the alt-right racist provocateurs who attended the rally were the future of the GOP. Pareene noted:

Racial resentment has been a driving force behind College Republican recruitment for years, but at this point it’s really all they have left to offer. In the age of President Donald Trump, what inspires a young person not merely to be conservative or vote Republican, but to get active in organized Republican politics? Do you think it’s a fervent belief that Paul Ryan knows the optimal tax policy to spur economic growth? Or do you think it’s more likely to be something else?

Pareene ended his essay by naming one rally attendee:

These future Republican elected officials could easily look very much like rally attendee Nicholas Fuentes, a Boston University student until his decision this week to leave the school. He didn’t appear to be a formal member of any young Republican organizations, but he was a self-described Republican. In interviews, he denies being a white supremacist. On Facebook, after the rally, he wrote: “The rootless transnational elite knows that a tidal wave of white identity is coming.”

In 2017, Fuentes was, to borrow a Bob Dylan phrase, a complete unknown, a college dropout with some local notoriety for his racist provocations. But he would shortly become one of the most popular streamers on the far right, infamous for his repeated Holocaust denial and praise of Nazism. Both Trump and his vice president JD Vance have been diligent about cultivating the hard-core racists in their coalition, including Fuentes, who infamously dined with Trump and Kanye West at Mar-a-Lago in 2022.

We’re now a decade into Trump’s takeover of the GOP. It ill-behoves us at this late date to be shocked by the fact that a Trump acolyte like Mike Collins has said bigoted things, has bigoted family members, and has repeatedly hired bigots for his staff. Collins does all this because this is how you succeed in GOP politics.

title: Trump Is Waging War on Haitians
description: Sasha...
fullText:
In Springfield, Ohio, ICE agents are targeting a community that Trump has been villainizing since 2024.

Late last week, volunteers working with the Haitian community in Springfield, Ohio, were inundated with calls about men being arrested and separated from their families. One of those detained was a pastor, Gilbert Joubert Adrien. Joubert Adrien, who is the minister of a church of 130 people, was, apparently, snatched by ICE agents while at a gas station. He is just one of several dozen Haitians to be targeted by ICE in Springfield in the past week, according to monitoring groups such as G92 and the Haitian Bridge Alliance.

Haitians in Springfield have been the center of some of the cruelest xenophobic behaviors of the Trump era. Perhaps you will remember the 2024 presidential campaign, during which JD Vance and Donald Trump made up false rumors about Haitians in the city “eating dogs and cats.” Trump doubled down on this outlandish claim during his televised debate with Kamala Harris; Vance admitted that the allegations were likely false but nevertheless went out of his way to justify his circulation of these slanderous allegations.

Now the administration is unleashing the full force of ICE on this same community, launching what can only be described as an officially sanctioned pogrom against people whose offense seems mainly to be that they are members of a race and a nation that Trump regards with peculiar contempt and animus. “These are people who fled for their lives,” Guerline Jozef, of the Haitian Bridge Alliance told me. “Some of them still have pending asylum claims, which means the government is violating due process.”

Similar attacks against Haitians are occurring around the country. In San Diego, advocates for the Haitian community have been using social media to report dozens of ICE kidnappings over the past two weeks along El Cajon Boulevard, and in the City Heights and Lemon Grove neighborhoods. In Flatbush, Brooklyn, the epicenter of the Big Apple’s Haitian community, businesses report that fewer customers are coming in, with community members afraid to be seen in public lest ICE snatch them. In the days after the Supreme Court ruling, the New York City Public Advocate’s office reported increased ICE activity in the neighborhood. In southern Florida, the Haitian Bridge Alliance reports that a surge of immigrants Haitians have been arrested and placed into deportation proceedings since the Supreme Court ruling. Jozef tells me of Haitian meatpackers and poultry workers in Salisbury, Maryland, and Virginia, who have also been snatched by ICE. She marvels, she says at “the cruelty, the inhumanity, the terror in what they are inflicting on the community.” And, she says, the Alliance expects things to only get worse, “even more casualties, more cruelties, more children being left without their parents.”

During Trump 1.0, the MAGA leader listed Haiti among the “shithole” countries of the world whose people he didn’t want immigrating to the US. One of the immediate consequences of Trump’s loathing of Haitians was a shutting of the southern border to Haitian men traveling north after they had been booted out of Brazil during a particular moment of economic crisis. In 2018, I interviewed many Haitian women in San Diego who had been stranded in the city with their young children, while their husbands, boyfriends, and teenage sons were either detained in US detention centers after asking for asylum or were stuck in limbo in Tijuana and unable to reunite with their female relatives in the United States.

Fast-forward eight years and that animus is, at speed, upending hundreds of thousands of lives and causing untold economic chaos in communities around the United States. It goes without saying that the vast majority of the more than 300,000 Haitians Trump is targeting around the country are law-abiding members of society. Until the US Supreme Court’s hard-right majority allowed the administration to shred Haitians’ Temporary Protected Status, they were living and working in the country entirely legally, working in industries such as home healthcare and construction, in restaurants and warehouses. They had the required work permits and they had Social Security numbers. Now their papers have been deemed void, in a way not dissimilar to how German Jews were deprived of citizenship rights in the early years of Nazi rule; their status has been revoked, and they are being quite literally hunted by ICE, fitted with ankle monitors, or simply thrown into harsh detention centers. Many of them are being summarily flown back to Haiti—a country with a supposedly transitional government presided over by an unelected council, which has no democratic mandate and that exists largely in name only, its writ hardly present in many parts of the nation; afflicted with desperate poverty; and experiencing daily terror inflicted by some of the most violent gangs on earth—and left to fend for themselves however they can.

In a single day’s haul last week, ICE deported more than 160 people back to Haiti, according to reporting by the Miami Herald. They were dropped off in Port-au-Prince with nothing but their wits to survive on. Days later, gangs in the nearby city of Kenscoff killed 47 people and kidnapped many others—further evidence, if any were needed, of just how dangerous conditions are in the country that these deportees are now being sent to. Instead of pulling back, the administration doubled down. On Thursday, the The New York Times reported that team Trump was planning weekly deportation flights to Haiti.The real risk of violent death faced by these deportees is, clearly, of absolutely no concern to the masters of Trump’s deportation machine.

It is hard to overemphasize just how authoritarian and cruel this all is. In its vast scale, we can liken it to Stalin’s projects of uprooting hundreds of thousands and millions at a go, and ordering them to relocate without consideration for impact on families or on community. It is, too, redolent of some early Nazi practices: In the deliberate humiliation ritual of fitting law-abiding people, recently deemed enemies of the state, with ankle monitors—all-too-visible markers of “otherness”—simply because of who they are, it is redolent of the Nazi’s decision, early in Hitler’s reign, to force Jews to wear the identifying tag of the yellow Star of David sewn onto their clothing.

Good Germans, back then, either turned a blind eye to what was happening, cheered it on, or, if they were government officials, rationalized the implementation of these vile mandates by avowing that they were only obeying orders. Today, I fear, Good Americans are doing much the same thing: Some simply prefer not to see; others—the MAGA diehards—cheer on this sadism; and still others, including those working for government agencies that are increasingly made dirty by Trump’s fanaticism, rationalize the unjustifiable by saying that this is all above their pay grade and that they are simply doing what they have been ordered to do.

There is, in the United States these days, more than a whiff of Hannah Arendt’s banality of evil. Entirely atrocious things—things that will haunt subsequent generations—are being done in our names; yet the temptation is that we get on with our daily lives and ignore the screams of terror and of despair from the victims of Trump’s unleashed gestapo.

title: Patriots Work Out Veteran Specialist Amid Punter Uncertainty
description: New England reportedly evaluated another experienced option after an injury created sudden uncertainty at punter.
fullText:
Patriots Work Out Veteran Specialist Amid Punter Uncertainty originally appeared on NESN. 

The New England Patriots are exploring another potential solution to their unexpected uncertainty at punter. New England worked out veteran Jamie Gillan on Thursday, according to the NFL transaction wire, as first noted by Pats Pulpit. The visit came before the Patriots closed their preseason schedule against the Cleveland Browns, the team Gillan began his NFL career with in 2019.

Gillan's workout was notable because Bryce Baringer suffered an injury during New England's second preseason game. The Patriots already signed veteran Matt Haack to provide immediate depth, but their interest in Gillan showed they were continuing to examine the available options. Baringer's absence created an unusual scene against the Philadelphia Eagles. Rookie quarterback Behren Morton was forced to handle a punt after Baringer left the game.

New England understandably did not want to repeat that situation.

MORE: Patriots Star A.J. Brown, Wife Announce Exciting Family News

Gillan, nicknamed "The Scottish Hammer," has appeared in 107 NFL games across six seasons.

The 29-year-old signed with Cleveland as an undrafted free agent out of Arkansas-Pine Bluff in 2019. He earned AFC Special Teams Player of the Week, AFC Special Teams Player of the Month and PFWA All-Rookie honors during his first season. Gillan spent three years with the Browns before briefly joining the Buffalo Bills' practice squad. He then served as the New York Giants' punter from 2022 through the 2025 season before being released in March.

The Scotland native has averaged 45.2 yards per punt and 40.3 net yards per punt during his career. His longest attempt traveled 74 yards, and 162 of his 436 punts have been downed inside the opponent's 20-yard line. Gillan also is a left-footed punter, which could provide New England with a different option if Baringer is not ready for the beginning of the regular season.

Haack remains the more immediate answer. The well-traveled veteran has played for the Miami Dolphins, Bills, Indianapolis Colts, Browns and Giants. His experience as both a punter and holder made him a sensible late-preseason addition. Working out Gillan does not guarantee the Patriots will sign him. NFL teams routinely evaluate free agents to update their emergency lists, particularly around the roster reduction deadline.

The visit nevertheless confirmed that New England was not leaving anything to chance.

The Patriots entered the summer expecting Baringer to handle their punting duties. His injury forced them to adjust quickly, and Gillan now represents another experienced option if the uncertainty continues into the regular season.

title: Ex-Raiders RB Faces Criminal Charges as Potential NFL Suspension Looms
description: Former Las Vegas Raiders running back Josh Jacobs has been formally charged after an alleged domestic violence incident. The post Ex-Raiders RB Faces Criminal Charges as Potential NFL Suspension Looms appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
Former Las Vegas Raiders running back Josh Jacobs has been formally charged after an alleged domestic violence incident at his home in May.

Jacobs was initially accused of grabbing the arm of a woman identified as his girlfriend during a struggle in their home. He was charged on Thursday by prosecutors in Wisconsin, facing two misdemeanor charges related to the incident.

As ESPN reported, Jacobs was charged with misdemeanor battery and misdemeanor criminal damage to property.

"Our office sought to ensure a fair and complete review of available evidence, some of which only recently became available to our office due to significant, ongoing forensic efforts by law enforcement," Brown County District Attorney David L. Lasee said in a statement. "A criminal complaint is nothing more than a written, formal accusation against a defendant alleging the commission of criminal offenses and does not raise any inference of guilt. Mr. Jacobs is presumed innocent of these charges. As this is an ongoing criminal case, and out of respect for the rights of all parties, our office will not have further comment on the matter at this time."

Jacobs could risk nine months in prison and a fine of up to $10,000 for each charge if convicted.

The running back's lawyers released a statement noting that police did not formally charge him with domestic violence.

"The Brown County District Attorney has reviewed evidence and elected to file misdemeanor charges against Josh that do not include domestic violence," noted the lawyers, David Z. Chesnoff, Richard A. Schonfeld and Clarence F. Duchac III. "The allegations will be addressed in court, and not in the media. Mr. Jacobs respects the District Attorney's office and the process it followed."

Jacobs started his NFL career with the Raiders in 2019 and had success as the team's running back, leading the NFL in 2022 with 1,653 rushing yards. He joined the Packers in 2024.

Jacobs is set to make a court appearance on Nov. 17.

As ESPN noted, the league is investigating the allegations and could suspend Jacobs either to start the season or once his court case has concluded. The league has wide latitude to issue punishment in cases of alleged domestic violence, even if charges are ultimately dropped.

The Packers said they would continue to cooperate with the NFL during the investigation, but would not comment further on the charges.

title: Chargers player lands on chopping block among veterans ahead of cuts
description: This Chargers veteran offensive lineman is among the potential players who could be cut before the 53-man rosters are finalized.
fullText:
The Chargers are a few weeks away from the start of what should be an exciting and thrilling 2026 season.

Los Angeles has set itself up for a great season and should be in the thick of things in the AFC West and the conference. However, before all that takes place, the Chargers will cut down their roster from 90 players to 53.

That is all set to take place on August 30, and there will be some tough decisions to make from now until then. Usually, undrafted young players or fringe NFL guys get cut more often than not; however, veteran offensive lineman Trevor Penning is a prime candidate for the chopping block.

Carter Bahns of CBS Sports listed 20 veterans who could be cut, and Penning was among them.

"Los Angeles' maligned offensive line is now mostly healthy and rebuilt, so there is less need for Penning, who would be nothing more than a second-teamer if he stuck on the roster. Considering all it cost to get him was a sixth-round pick, the Chargers can easily cut bait."

Penning is a former first-round pick in 2022 by the Saints and spent the 2025 season with the Chargers. The 27-year-old re-signed with the Bolts on a one-year deal in March 2026.

It's been tough for Penning in Los Angeles due to a variety of reasons. For starters, he has struggled with pass protection, frequent penalties, and adjusting to multiple position shifts on an injury-depleted offensive line.

The Chargers' offensive line has plenty of questions entering the season, especially after losing center Tyler Biadasz. The uncertainty doesn't stop there, as the interior offensive line remains unsettled.

Even so, there's a chance Penning will look for a new team by next week.

This article originally appeared on Chargers Wire: Chargers player lands on chopping block among veterans ahead of cuts

title: Kevin Durant looks back on the 2021 Nets team that he felt was the best team on paper
description: It seems Kevin Durant is still sad his Nets stint did not work out.
fullText:
Kevin Durant looks back on the 2021 Nets team that he felt was the best team on paper originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

Having Kevin Durant, Kyrie Irving, and James Harden on the same team would have been a cheat code for any team. The Brooklyn Nets thought they had finally unlocked the puzzle, as they had a big three ready to win a championship.

Unfortunately, it all fizzled out without a title. It was a big blow to the Nets and the trio because they could not meet their goal. To this day, Durant is hurt by what happened because he thought it was the best team he had ever played on.

It is a bold statement to make because Durant was part of the Golden State Warriors team that won the 2017 and 2018 championships. In fact, to this day, people think that Warriors squad was one of the best in NBA history, especially the 2017 team that only lost one game in the Playoffs.

The 2021/22 Nets team was loaded with talent, especially on the top level with the trio of Durant, Irving, and Harden. Unfortunately, they could not beat the injury bug. They only played 16 games together, and during that stretch, they went 13-3, which was split into 8-2 in the regular season and 5-1 in the Playoffs.

MORE: Inside the history of postseason disappointments with James Harden's career

If they were all healthy, they could have easily won the championship. Unfortunately, that was not the case due to the injuries and Harden getting traded to the Philadelphia 76ers in February 2022. It was a messy situation for all parties involved, which made Durant always wonder what could have been.

"That's the biggest one for me; it would've been so dope to see that in Brooklyn. Just looking at the straight roster, and nothing else, I would say Brooklyn. Blake Griffin, LaMarcus Aldridge, Paul Millsap, Patty Mills. We had the names on that team when you're looking at straight paper," Durant said on Boardroom about the best team on paper during his playing career.

It is a fair assessment because they did have a lot of talented players. Of course, there was context behind all of them, but when looking at the names, it is fair to call them the best. A lot of people will deem the Warriors teams as the best on paper, but Durant feels like the Nets had the better group based on name recognition alone.
