title: Twins calling up top prospect Walker Jenkins amid Byron Buxton injury concerns
description: Buxton has battled a hip injury throughout the season, putting him on the injured list twice since July 4.
fullText:
The Minnesota Twins are calling up top prospect Walker Jenkins for this weekend's series with the Chicago White Sox amid uncertainty regarding Byron Buxton's availability due to a hip injury. The team announced the move Thursday.

Jenkins, 21, had a .308/.407/.532 slash line with Triple-A St. Paul, adding 12 home runs, 17 doubles, 28 RBI and 17 stolen bases in 307 plate appearances while dealing with hamstring and shoulder injuries. In August, he is slashing .411/.488/.795 with 8 home runs and 7 steals.

Ranked as Minnesota's No. 1 prospect by MLB.com (and No. 15 overall), Jenkins was the Twins' 2023 first-round draft pick (fifth overall) out of South Brunswick High School in North Carolina.

Walker Jenkins homers for the third time in his past three games.

The @Twins' top prospect skies his 14th of the year -- his 12th for the Triple-A @StPaulSaints: pic.twitter.com/lCyVrHbv0Z

Buxton, 32, aggravated a right hip injury in Tuesday's 4-2 loss to the Athletics while running and reaching down for a hit into the right-center gap during the seventh inning. Following the triple by Henry Bolte, Buxton was in obvious discomfort, favoring his right leg and came out of the game.

The 12-year veteran has been limited to 93 games this season because of a right hip impingement. The issue has resulted in two stints on the injured list, making Buxton available for only nine games from July 4 to Aug. 13.

Byron Buxton was removed from the game with an injury after reaching down for a ball in the outfield pic.twitter.com/rVZiRD71d4

When he's been in the lineup, Buxton has been productive with a .254/.319/.511 slash average with 25 home runs, 22 doubles and 46 RBI in 408 PAs. He's also played well in center field according to advanced metrics, crediting him with 1 Defensive Run Saved and 3 Outs Above Average.

No corresponding move for Jenkins' call-up has yet been announced, so Buxton returning to the IL for a third time is not a certainty.

Jenkins is the second top prospect that the Twins have called up in August, joining shortstop Kaelen Culpepper.

At 64-70, the Twins are four games back from the American League's third wild-card playoff spot. However, five teams are ahead of them in the standings, including the Cleveland Guardians who currently hold that third spot at 68-66.

Trailing the Chicago White Sox by 6.5 games in the AL Central, the wild card is likely the only parth for Minnesota to get to the postseason.

title: Chiefs Take A Significant Tumble In Watchability List
description: The Kansas City Chiefs were tough to watch last year, and this list reflects how much they've fallen.
fullText:
The Kansas City Chiefs used to be must-see TV, with a high-flying offense that featured quarterback Patrick Mahomes, receiver Tyreek Hill and an offense that was a non-stop scoring machine.

Those days are gone, though, and Ben Solak of ESPN rated the Chiefs 22nd in a piece rating each team according to what he called their "watchability." It's a shocking rating that says a lot about how much things have changed in Kansas City as Solak backed up his rating with some solid points.

Start with the fact that the Chiefs don't create explosive plays anymore, as they only did this 9.3 percent of the time, per Solak, which puts them at 26th in the league last year. They also don't give them up, which speaks to how much the Chiefs have shifted to become a defensive team since the Hill trade as Mahomes' cap hit has continued to grow.

The Chiefs do play in a lot of close games, which is a point in their favor, and usually those games are entertaining. They were anything but for Chiefs fans last season, as they went just 1-9 last season, and by the end of the year Kansas City was nearly unwatchable without Mahomes.

The Chiefs are trying to remedy all this, of course, but their solution may not be all that entertaining, either. They're putting Mahomes under center more and featuring new free agent running back Kenneth Walker III, with the goal of trying to take some of the heat off Mahomes as he continues to recover from knee surgery.

Kansas City believes Walker can break off some big runs, and there is some big-play capability oif the Chiefs can keep receiver Xavier Worthy on the field. Like many things, though, the Chiefs watchabilty factor will really be all about Mahomes.

The networks haven't given up on the Chiefs, however. Kansas City will be featured early and often, starting with their opener, which will be on Monday Night Football on Sept. 14.

What could redeem the Chiefs last year is those close games. Coach Andy Reid kept hoping Kansas City's luck would turn in those, as the Chiefs did have to deal with some tough breaks. Winning those games would make the Chiefs a lot more entertaining, altthough we'll miss the good old days of Mahomes running around making crazy plays.

But the Chiefs don't care about any of that, as they just want to win games in any way possible after last year's embarrassing 6-11 season.

title: Make No Mistake: A’s GM Gig Is A Desirable One
description: Something I’ve seen several times here is the notion that the A’s will have trouble luring a quality GM to be the next front office leader of the club. After all several openings will exist (we know for sure Houston is looking) and why would a GM choose the A’s, a nomadic team closing in […]
fullText:
Something I've seen several times here is the notion that the A's will have trouble luring a quality GM to be the next front office leader of the club. After all several openings will exist (we know for sure Houston is looking) and why would a GM choose the A's, a nomadic team closing in on 100 losses if they're not careful?

Glad you asked. To A's fans things might look bleak at the moment, as the team limps to the finish line in a season that has been epically disappointing. But to a GM coming on board, there is much to recommend the job:

1. A new stadium is imminent and that is always a terrific position for a franchise to be in. With the opening of a new stadium — and in this case also a new city location — comes excitement and the promise of a new revenue stream.

Now you and I may be as skeptical as we want as to how much Las Vegas will embrace the A's, how many of the fans will be die-hard A's fans and not tourists pulling hard for the opponent, whether all the games will be sold out or whether a small stadium will still struggle to fill every seat.

Nonetheless it's pretty much a given that attendance will be strong in the maiden years and that overall it will dwarf the numbers from Oakland and Sacramento, if only because those numbers were so small.

2. The core of young talent, for all its flaws and question marks, is in fact highly appealing. Nick Kurtz is already considered to be a star, Jacob Wilson has started an All-Star game, Shea Langeliers (3.6 fWAR in 2025) is considered one of the league's best catchers, and there's no denying the upside Lawrence Butler and Zack Gelof bring as they have displayed it in half season bursts. Henry Bolte has star potential as well and Brent Rooker is among those under contract for several more seasons.

It's also enviable to have Leo De Vries poised to debut sometime in 2027, getting his feet wet and hitting the ground running by the start of 2028. The pitching needs some attention, but Gage Jump, JT Ginn, and Jacob Lopez will soon be joined by Jamie Arnold and presumably Wei-En Lin will be back healthy by the time the A's christen their new stadium.

Of course there are no guarantees, but a lot of current GMs would like to have this talent to build around. There may need to be some changes in coaching and development staff to properly harness it, but a new GM has exactly that opportunity to make a footprint that can bring out the considerable upside seen in this young core.

3. The whole "Fisher won't spend" narrative is as tired as it is inaccurate. Fisher may pinch pennies when it comes to feeding minor leaguers during a pandemic, but he's also apparently putting out well over $1B to finish the stadium.

More to the point, regardless of why it is a fact that he is allowing for record contracts such as Luis Severino's $67M deal, numerous extensions in the tens of millions each, and increasing payroll overall. And this only figures to ramp up further as the A's try to create excitement in 2028.

Are there better gigs around MLB for a GM? Probably. Are there worse? Most certainly. On the continuum of "unappealing" to "appealing" I would submit that currently the A's rank right of the middle. A healthy 2027 A's team with added financial commitment both to the active roster and to the development side, could be exciting in its own right.

But with an eye to 2028 and beyond, a GM should be able to see tremendous potential to nurture a once proud franchise that intends to be proud again. Very soon. Under the right leadership.

title: Evaluating Jaguars' defensive depth chart before preseason finale
description: Heading into the final preseason game, let's project what the Jaguars' defensive depth chart might look like.
fullText:
With training camp now complete for the Jacksonville Jaguars, only one preseason game remains, a Friday night matchup with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

This contest will provide a number of players with one last opportunity to make their case for playing time or to make a roster push before cutdown day on Sunday.

So given what we've learned over the last month, here is our latest projection of the Jaguars' defensive depth chart.

Green and Striggow have seemingly established themselves as the next two defenders up in the edge rusher rotation. Williams should see some snaps, but as the potential fifth option, how many on a weekly basis remains to be seen.

Dickerson's consistency has helped him climb the depth chart. He is Armstead's backup, while Regis is the backup nose tackle. Orhorhoro provides an added pass rush presence.

Miller and Combs have been competing all summer for the starting role next to Oluokun. It's been difficult to gauge from the outside looking in who has the upper hand. What I could see happening is the Jaguars rotate the two, with Miller on the field during running downs and Combs on the field during passing downs.

Another battle unfolding is McLeod, Tavai, and Abdullah for one potential roster spot. Each has flashed this summer, so knowing exactly where things stand between the three isn't easy to decipher. Tavai's experience on defense and teams could be a differentiator for him.

I think that Muhammad has established himself as the fifth cornerback with his consistent play dating back to offseason programs. The question here, perhaps, is whether or not Braswell makes the roster as the sixth cornerback or whether the Jaguars roster only five?

We've known for a while that the first five players listed were going to make up the safety room on the 53-man roster. My one change after watching the first two preseason games is I placed Huskey ahead of Lane. He's really flashed on defense.

title: MLB Attempts To Tie Limited Free Agent Signing Period To Competitive Balance
description: MLB offered a new proposal as part of the latest collective bargaining sessions that would create a limited free agent signing period, but only contingent on a salary cap.
fullText:
On Thursday, Major League Baseball made its latest proposal to the MLB Players Association for the next collective bargaining agreement. It would create an extreme shift in the free agent signing period, looking to mirror other sports by placing a strict limit on the window in which signings could take place, creating a frenzied period designed to increase fan interest.

As first reported by MLB.com, the five days after the World Series would still allow players and clubs to trigger or decline options. After that, free agents would be allowed to negotiate deals, but signings would only be allowed after 12 p.m. on the Monday of the first day of the Winter Meetings through December 21st. From Dec. 21st through the first Monday in February, no free agent signings or trades would be allowed. After the first Monday in February, free agent signings would then be allowed to resume.

It is not the first time that the league has sought to have a limited free agent signing period. The league proposed it as part of the negotiations of the current labor deal in place since 2021, and as recently as January, MLB Commissioner Rob Manfred discussed it on WFAN, touting it as a way to promote excitement.

"I think there's going to be some more conversation about it, because I do believe that there's a marketing opportunity," Manfred said. "Let's face it, we operate in a really competitive environment. Just put entertainment, generally, to one side — just sports, right? It's really competitive. And I think that you make a mistake, particularly during the offseason, when you don't take every advantage to push your sport out in front of your fans during that down period."

An important change in direction with the latest proposal is that the league has suddenly shifted and is tying it to implementing a salary cap. That was not the case in negotiations for the current labor deal, nor did Manfred mention it on WFAN in January.

When asked why the proposal on Thursday could not be offered separately from MLB's push for a cap system, MLB spokesperson Glen Caplin said, "In our current economic system, these changes would be too harmful to competitive balance and would not be practical."

As The Athletic reported in January, player agents see the limited signing period differently.

Scott Boras, who has notoriously used the start of Spring Training to leverage deals for his players, sees the proposal negatively.

"The sole purpose of deadlines (is to) simply restrict competition and deny players the true market," Boras said. "Our current rules allow for ultimate roster construction and the best possible team for a season. (A deadline is) not for competition reasons. Every owner wants the opportunity for time to allow him to respond to changes by his competitors. That's why there's been many significant signings 

Other agents, notably Joel Wolfe, head of the Wasserman's baseball division, have seen limited signing windows work with international players from Japan.

"If there was a way to re-create the exceptional efficiency of the posting system for all the free agents, I would certainly be interested in that," said Wolfe, who represents Los Angeles Dodgers pitchers Roki Sasaki and Yoshinobu Yamamoto to The Athletic. "But I have yet to see a good answer as to what happens to the FA's if they go unsigned that doesn't unfairly prejudice them. MLB teams always seem to find a way to game the system and crush a large part of the class. I think it's worth exploring.

"I just haven't seen any great idea yet that benefits all the players."

The proposal on Thursday to limit the free agent signing period and tie it to the cap system garnered a pointed response from MLBPA interim Executive Director, Bruce Meyer.

"The league, through their propaganda arm, is promoting their latest set of roster and transaction proposals as player-friendly," said Meyer. "MLB expressly conditioned these proposals on the players' agreement to a salary cap system, which would drastically reduce overall player compensation, eliminate fully guaranteed contracts through escrow, and turn back the clock on fundamental player rights."

"Their latest proposals regarding free agency would eliminate Player rights by establishing an artificial free agency window, subject to a salary cap, which would reduce player leverage and create a game of musical chairs pitting player vs. player."

"The suggestion that the only way to limit roster churn, or incentivize earlier Free Agent signings is with a salary cap is entirely unserious. Players have proposed changes that would address these priorities, but the league is not interested in any changes that don't directly reduce the rights of all players and shift leverage to the owners."

The current labor deal between MLB and the players is set to expire at 11:59 pm ET on December 1st. If the owners and players do not agree on a new deal by then, the owners are expected to lock out the players. If so, the Baseball Winter Meetings would be canceled, and all player transactions – either trades or free agent signings – would stop until a new labor deal is reached.

The 2027 MLB regular season is scheduled to start on the night of Wednesday, March 24th.

This article was originally published on Forbes.com

title: 49ers insider weighs in on possibility 49ers are sold by Jed York
description: NBC Sports Bay Area's Matt Maiocco's doesn't think Jed York's arrest will change the way he views the ownership of the 49ers.
fullText:
The fallout from owner Jed York's arrest continues to hang over the San Francisco 49ers, but NBC Sports Bay Area's Matt Maiocco doesn't believe it will cost the York family the franchise.

York was charged with two misdemeanors — disorderly conduct and possession of criminal tools — after responding to an undercover ad on what was described as a known prostitution website. He received a two-day jail sentence and a $1,150 fine. NFL commissioner Roger Goodell confirmed at the league's preseason owners' meeting that the incident is being reviewed under the personal conduct policy. York did not attend the meeting, a decision that wasn't surprising given how recent the arrest was.

Speaking on KNBR, Maiocco addressed the inevitable speculation about a forced sale directly, pointing to how deliberately the York family structured its ownership just two years ago.

"I can't see that. Jed bought equity from his mom in order to become the principal owner. Yes, the 49ers raised a lot of money by selling off around 9.7% of the organization, but when they transferred ownership officially over to Jed as the principal owner, the idea was this was a move made to ensure that it remained in the family," Maiocco said. "I would imagine the long-term plan is for Jed to hand it over to one of his sons or keep it in the family. I don't think this [arrest] will impact that. I think that there will be some discipline by commissioner Roger Goodell. I think it can happen sooner rather than later because the legal process has run its course. I would expect a fine and even a suspension, where he has to stay away from the team for a certain amount of time."

York became the 49ers' principal owner in March 2024, purchasing additional equity from his family specifically to formalize what had effectively been his role since taking over as CEO in 2010. At the time, York did frame the move as a long-term succession plan, saying it was "reflective of how we've operated" and intended to keep the team "in our family for generations to come." His mother, Denise DeBartolo York, and father, Dr. John York, remained co-chairs.

Maiocco acknowledged the situation is embarrassing for the organization and could become a talking point if the 49ers stumble out of the gate, but he drew a comparison to another franchise that weathered owner controversy without a sale: the New England Patriots under Robert Kraft.

"Nobody was talking about that with Robert Kraft," Maiocco said, "and I think it'll blow over, but it will always be kind of in the back of people's minds."

This article originally appeared on Niners Wire: 49ers insider weighs in on possibility 49ers are sold by Jed York

title: Today in sports history, September 21
description: Today in sports history, September 21
fullText:
Today is Sept. 21. On this date in:

1892: John Clarkson of the Cleveland Spiders defeated Pittsburgh 3-2 to become the fifth pitcher in major league history to reach 300 career victories.

1896: Connie Mack announced he would leave Pittsburgh to manage Milwaukee in the Western League, a career move that preceded his legendary tenure as an owner and executive with the Athletics.

1933: The Washington Senators defeated the St. Louis Browns 2-1 to clinch the American League pennant.

1934: St. Louis Cardinals rookie Paul "Daffy" Dean pitched a no-hitter in a 3-0 victory over the Brooklyn Dodgers, completing a doubleheader sweep after his brother Dizzy Dean threw a three-hit shutout in the opener.

1955: Rocky Marciano recovered from a second-round knockdown and stopped Archie Moore in the ninth round at Yankee Stadium to retain the heavyweight championship. Marciano retired the following year with a 49-0 record.

1961: The Minnesota Twins defeated the Washington Senators 6-3 in the final major league game at Griffith Stadium in Washington.

1963: Pittsburgh Pirates coach Gene Baker became the first Black person to take charge of a major league team when he managed the final two innings after manager Danny Murtaugh and coach Frank Oceak were ejected against the Los Angeles Dodgers.

1969: New York Jets punter Steve O'Neal launched a 98-yard punt against the Denver Broncos, setting an NFL record that still stands.

1970: The Cleveland Browns defeated the New York Jets 31-21 in the inaugural "Monday Night Football" regular-season telecast on ABC.

1971: American League owners approved the relocation of the Washington Senators to Arlington, Texas, clearing the way for the franchise that became the Texas Rangers.

1978: San Diego Padres pitcher Gaylord Perry defeated the San Francisco Giants 5-1 for his 20th victory, reaching the mark for the fifth time in his career.

1981: Philadelphia Phillies pitcher Steve Carlton struck out 12 Montreal Expos and surpassed Bob Gibson as the National League's career strikeout leader.

1982: NFL players began a strike that suspended the season for 57 days and reduced each team's schedule from 16 games to nine.

1985: Michael Spinks defeated Larry Holmes by unanimous decision in Las Vegas to capture the heavyweight championship and end Holmes' undefeated reign.

1990: Oakland's Bob Welch became the first major league pitcher in 12 years to reach 25 victories in a season.

2001: In the first major sporting event in New York after the Sept. 11 terrorist attacks, Mike Piazza hit a dramatic eighth-inning home run to lift the Mets past the Atlanta Braves 3-2 at Shea Stadium.

2008: The New York Yankees defeated the Baltimore Orioles 7-3 in the final game at the original Yankee Stadium, which had opened in 1923.

2008: The United States defeated Europe 16½-11½ at Valhalla Golf Club to win the Ryder Cup and snap a streak of three consecutive European victories.

2014: Lewis Hamilton won the Singapore Grand Prix and took the Formula One championship lead while equaling Juan Manuel Fangio's mark of eight Grand Prix victories for Mercedes.

2019: Manchester City defeated Watford 8-0 for the largest top-flight victory in club history and became the first Premier League team to lead 5-0 after 18 minutes.

2024: The Chicago White Sox lost their 119th game, tying the 2003 Detroit Tigers' American League record for losses in a season.

title: Why is the Astros-Yankees Game Delayed Today? When Will it Start?
description: Why is the Astros-Yankees game delayed today? Here’s the reason for the delay and the latest update on when the game is expected to start. The post Why is the Astros-Yankees Game Delayed Today? When Will it Start? appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The Bronx is bracing for a soaked ballgame. After rain suspended play in the U.S. Open across town in Queens, showers halted Thursday's Astros-Yankees rubber match at Yankee Stadium, with first pitch originally set for 7:05 p.m. ET.

New York enters the night holding down a wild card cushion it can't afford to squander, and any lost innings threaten to complicate an already strained pitching staff heading into the stretch run.

But the delay looks to be a quick one, at least that's what the Yankeespredict. At 6:23 p.m. theteam posted, "Please be advised, tonightâs first pitch will be at 7:15 p.m."

That would be a delay of only 10 minutes, if the Yankees' announced new start time holds.

Forecasters had flagged the danger well before first pitch. A 51% chance of rain accompanied the 7:05 p.m. window at Yankee Stadium, according to RotoWire, with 10 mph winds blowing right to left and temperatures near 77 degrees.

A Flood Watch remains in effect for the Bronx through 11 p.m., with daytime showers and thunderstorms carrying a 70% chance before transitioning to roughly 40% overnight. Dewpoints near 68 degrees kept the atmosphere primed for heavy downpours if storms redeveloped near first pitch.

NEW YORK YANKEES STARTING LINEUP

SP: Gerrit Cole (RHP) • 7-6, 3.11 ERA

August 27, 2026 • Yankee Stadium, Bronx, NY • 7:05 PM EDT • Astros at Yankees

Lineups confirmed. Season stats shown (AVG / SLG).

The National Weather Service warned some storms could turn severe through the evening, with a 60% chance of precipitation and rainfall totals up to three-quarters of an inch possible in the Bronx.

Right-hander Gerrit Cole was lined up to start for New York, working off a strong outing last time out. Cole allowed one earned run on four hits over six innings against Baltimore, pushing his season ERA down to 3.11 with a 1.068 WHIP, according to a Bleacher Nation report. A long delay risks disrupting his rhythm. A stoppage mid-game usually ends a starter's night altogether.

SP: Hayden Wesneski (RHP) • 3-1, 4.23 ERA

August 27, 2026 • Yankee Stadium, Bronx, NY • 7:05 PM EDT • Astros at Yankees

Lineups confirmed. Season stats shown (AVG / SLG).

New York carries a 75-57 record into the series finale, sitting comfortably in the American League's wild card standings picture But the Yankees' rotation is hurting. Max Fried, Clarke Schmidt and Ryan Weathers are all sidelined with elbow or forearm injuries, and high-leverage reliever Fernando Cruz remains out as well and may need Tommy John surgery, leaving the Yankees with little margin if a delay forces excess bullpen innings tonight.

Houston, at 66-67, brings right-hander Hayden Wesneski to the mound, set to start for the Astros in his sixth outing of the season, having thrown five scoreless innings in his last appearance against the Athletics. Wesneski carries a 4.23 ERA and 22 strikeouts across 27 2/3 innings on the year.

The Astros are locked in a tight battle atop the American League West, sitting a half-game up on Texas, meaning every game against the Yankees is make-or-break for a club that can't afford a lost outing from its rotation. A delay tonight would ripple into Houston's next series against the Mets.

New York, meanwhile, has won 11 of its last 17 games and owns the best team ERA in the majors at roughly 3.23. The Yankees also open a home series against Boston on Friday, with a doubleheader already on the schedule from an earlier rainout, meaning any further disruption tonight compounds a workload problem that's been building for weeks.

A pure rain delay would keep Thursday's game on the books for the same calendar day, with tickets remaining valid once play resumes. A postponement is a different animal entirely, pushing the contest to a makeup date that could mean a doubleheader or an extra grind on both bullpens already feeling the innings pile up in late August.

title: Inter Miami name Kily González head coach
description: Miami CF have named Cristian 'Kily' González as their new head coach, the club announced Thursday The 52-year-old former Argentine international officially replaces his ex-Alb...
fullText:
Inter Miami CF have named Cristian 'Kily' González as their new head coach, the club announced Thursday

The 52-year-old former Argentine international officially replaces his ex-Albiceleste teammate Javier Mascherano, who departed the club in April.

The Herons had been led by Guillermo Hoyos, who will remain charge of the team until the arrival of the new head coach and his coaching staff.

González joins Miami with a half-decade of coaching experience in his native Argentina, most recently with Club Atlético Platense during the 2025 Primera División season.

He began his first-team managerial career at boyhood club Rosario Central (2020-22) before taking the reins at Unión Santa Fe between 2023-25.

As a player, González starred for the likes of Rosario Central, Boca Juniors, Real Zaragoza, Valencia and Inter Milan. He represented Argentina at the 2002 FIFA World Cup and helped his country win gold at the 2004 Summer Olympic Games.

González takes over a Miami side led by Argentina legend Lionel Messi and an A-list supporting cast highlighted by fellow global superstars Luis Suárez, Rodrigo De Paul and Casemiro.

Since Messi's summer 2023 arrival, the Herons have won three titles: Leagues Cup 2023, the 2024 MLS Supporters' Shield and MLS Cup 2025 presented by Audi.

The first-ever back-to-back Landon Donovan MLS MVP (2024, '25), Messi has 14g/9a this season while also guiding Argentina, along with De Paul, to the 2026 World Cup final.

Miami are second in the Eastern Conference with 39 points. They're looking to become the first repeat MLS Cup champions since the LA Galaxy in 2011-12.

title: Patriots Speedster Pulls Off Eye-Opening Preseason Feat
description: Kyle Williams did something in all three Patriots preseason games that no New England coach could ignore.
fullText:
Patriots Speedster Pulls Off Eye-Opening Preseason Feat originally appeared on NESN. 

The New England Patriots kept their starters wrapped in bubble wrap throughout the preseason, but Kyle Williams did not need the first-team offense around him to make a major impression.

Williams capped his impressive August by scoring a touchdown in New England's preseason finale against the Cleveland Browns on Thursday night. The explosive receiver hauled in a pass from Tommy DeVito and raced 45 yards to the end zone for the Patriots' first score of the game.

The play continued a remarkable streak for Williams, who scored a touchdown in each of New England's three preseason games.

That is one way to make sure nobody forgets about you. Williams finished the first half against Cleveland with two receptions for 55 yards and a touchdown. His 45-yard score offered another reminder of the speed and big-play ability he can bring to New England's offense when the games begin to count.

Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel took a cautious approach throughout the exhibition schedule. New England did not play its starters in any of its three preseason games, leaving Williams to work with reserve quarterbacks and a constantly changing supporting cast. That could have made it difficult for the young receiver to generate much momentum.

Kyle Williams too easy 💨💨💨 pic.twitter.com/B23Tb1Fi2j

Instead, Williams consistently found ways to stand out.

He reached the end zone in the preseason opener, did it again against the Philadelphia Eagles and completed the three-game sweep in Cleveland. Scoring in every preseason game does not guarantee regular-season success, but it certainly demonstrates Williams' ability to capitalize on limited opportunities. His explosiveness was the most encouraging part.

Williams does not need to pile up receptions to change a game. He has the speed to turn one opening into a touchdown, as he showed by breaking loose against the Browns. That trait could make him especially valuable to an offense looking for more chunk plays.

The Patriots did not reveal much about their regular-season plans during the preseason. Their starting quarterback, offensive line and top skill players remained on the sideline, making it nearly impossible to evaluate what the full offense will look like. Williams still managed to provide a compelling preview.

MORE: Patriots Work Out Veteran Specialist Amid Punter Uncertainty

New England has several receivers competing for roles, targets and roster positioning. Williams used his preseason opportunities to show that he offers something the offense badly needs: the ability to score from anywhere on the field.

There will be tougher tests against starting NFL defenses, and preseason production always should be viewed with some caution. Williams nevertheless did everything the Patriots could have asked of him.

Three games. Three touchdowns. One unmistakable message. The Patriots have an explosive weapon who deserves to be part of their regular-season plans.

title: Oklahoma State softball unveils fall schedule: Times, dates for 2026 OSU Cowgirls

fullText:
The Oklahoma State softball team released its fall slate on Thursday, with the Cowgirls set to compete in eight exhibition games.

OSU opens the fall with a home matchup against the University of Science and Arts of Oklahoma on Sept. 23.

The Cowgirls host Seminole State on Sept. 30 before hitting the road to face Wichita State on Oct. 4.

The Cowgirls then make a quick turnaround to host Oklahoma Christian on Oct. 8, followed by a visit to Langston on Oct. 11. Two days later, the Pokes host Oklahoma Baptist in their penultimate home game of the season.

A headlining battle with Arkansas in Fayetteville on Oct. 17 is one of the most anticipated fall games in all of college softball. The Razorbacks finished No. 4 in the country in 2026 after going 47-13 and earning a Women's College World Series berth.

Portland Trail Blazers guard Shaedon Sharpe is recovering from surgery to repair a meniscus tear in his right knee and will be evaluated again in about six months.

Sharpe, 23, who averaged a career-high 20.8 points per game last season, was injured during a workout last week.

He underwent the procedure Wednesday at the UCLA Department of Orthopedic Surgery and Sports Medicine, the team announced Thursday.

Sharpe also averaged 4.3 rebounds and 2.6 assists in 2025-26, helping Portland to its first postseason appearance since 2021 despite missing 32 games with a stress fracture of his left fibula.

title: Nuggets Make Decision on Contract of Jonas Valanciunas
description: The Denver Nuggets have made a salary-cap-related decision on the contract of former center Jonas Valanciunas.Valanciunas had a partial guarantee on the $10 million he was owed by the Nuggets for the 2026-27 season. However, after a mediocre performance as Nikola Jokic’s backup center in 2025-26, the Nuggets decided to pay him his partial guarantee […] The post Nuggets Make Decision on Contract of Jonas Valanciunas appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The Denver Nuggets have made a salary-cap-related decision on the contract of former center Jonas Valanciunas.

Valanciunas had a partial guarantee on the $10 million he was owed by the Nuggets for the 2026-27 season. However, after a mediocre performance as Nikola Jokic's backup center in 2025-26, the Nuggets decided to pay him his partial guarantee of $2 million instead of keeping him around for $10 million next year.

Now, they have made a salary-cap decision on that $2 million cap hit.

According to NBA reporter Michael Scotto of HoopsHype, the Nuggets decided to stretch the remaining $2 million left on Valanciunas' contract over the next three seasons, for a cap hit of $667,000 for each of the next three years.

"The Denver Nuggets are stretching Jonas Valanciunas' remaining $2 million salary owed for the 2026-27 season, league sources told @hoopshype . As a result, Valanciunas will be on Denver's books for $667K each of the following three seasons," Scotto wrote on X.

The Denver Nuggets are stretching Jonas Valanciunas’ remaining $2 million salary owed for the 2026-27 season, league sources told @hoopshype. As a result, Valanciunas will be on Denver’s books for $667K each of the following three seasons. https://t.co/2iecHUiwKy

— Michael Scotto (@MikeAScotto) August 27, 2026

While the Nuggets are still slightly over the second apron, by stretching this $2 million over the next three seasons, they significantly lowered their luxury tax hit.

According to HoopsRumors.com, the Nuggets will save approximately $9 million in luxury tax savings by stretching this deal, so you can understand why Denver's front office and ownership group decided to push the cap hit over the next three years.

With Valanciunas gone, the Nuggets signed veteran Marvin Bagley III to be Jokic's backup center next year.

Although Bagley was once considered a busted prospect, he had a good season split between the Washington Wizards and the Dallas Mavericks last season, and as a younger player, he should have the motor to give Denver the backup minutes that it seeks whenever Jokic needs a breather or is injured.

Bagley is only making $3.5 million this coming year on a cheap one-year flyer, so it was a solid move by the Nuggets, who will likely get superior production from him at a lower price compared to what the Nuggets would have had to pay Valanciunas before he was released by them.

description: The Los Angeles Rams and the Los Angeles Chargers play in their final tune-up contest
fullText:
The Los Angeles Rams "travel" to take on the Los Angeles Chargers in both team's final preseason game of the season. Not sure how to watch? Check out our how to watch guide!

title: Yankees Announce Decision on Former Top 10 Prospect Before Astros Game
description: The Yankees announced a decision involving a former top-10 prospect ahead of their game against the Houston Astros. The post Yankees Announce Decision on Former Top 10 Prospect Before Astros Game appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The New York Yankees send their ace, Gerrit Cole, to the mound Thursday â weather permitting â to try to nail down a series win against the American League West-leading Houston Astros, after the two teams split the first two contests of the three-game set.

With the Boston Red Sox idle, the Yankees have a chance to push their lead in the race for the top AL Wild Card spot to three full games over their arch-rivals.

Before the Astros game, the Yankees announced a decision on a roster move with one of their most prized pitching prospects, who only last year ranked as No. 9 in the New York system, per MLB Pipeline, before an arm injury requiring surgery set him back.

That pitcher is Chase Hampton, and Thursday's roster move had nothing to do with a new injury. The Yankees' Double-A affiliate activated the right-hander from the temporarily inactive list on August 27, 2026, according to MiLB.com's transaction records, ending an 18-day gap and returning him to Somerset's rotation. The move landed alongside other Double-A moves, including the promotions of Trent Sellers and Harrison Cohen from Triple-A and the assignment of Luis Velasquez to High-A Hudson Valley.

Hampton had been placed on the temporarily inactive list on August 9, according to the Somerset Patriots' team social media account. The designation typically covers short absences outside a standard injured list stint â family matters, personal circumstances, a brief developmental pause â rather than a new physical setback, and nothing in the transaction record points to a fresh injury.

GettyChase Hampton #86 of the New York Yankees.

Hampton's entire 2026 season has been about recovery. He underwent Tommy John surgery on his right elbow in February 2025, an operation that wiped out that whole campaign and followed a spring bullpen session that left him in discomfort, according to a CBS Sports report.

The rehab assignment stretched across three levels this year, from Single-A Tampa on May 8 to High-A Hudson Valley on May 26 to Somerset on June 12. The results since the return have been rough â an 0-6 record with an 8.19 ERA across 48.1 innings in 2026, according to Baseball Savant data, including a 9.93 ERA over nine starts at Double-A before this month's inactive-list stint.

Aubrey Chase Hampton was born in Longview, Texas, and grew up in nearby Kilgore. He pitched two seasons at Texas Tech before the Yankees popped him in the sixth round, 190th overall, in the 2022 draft, according to MLB Trade Rumors' Steve Adams.

His rise looked fast before the injuries piled up. In his 2023 professional debut, Hampton posted a 3.63 ERA with 145 strikeouts across 106.2 innings between High-A Hudson Valley and Double-A Somerset, pushing him as high as the organization's No. 4 overall prospect on some boards behind a fastball that touched 99 mph, plus a slider and curveball scouts have praised.

New York added him to the 40-man roster in November 2025, protecting him from the Rule 5 Draft. Adams described him at the time as a prospect who could pitch his way into a late-2026 look if he stayed healthy, though he called Hampton "a more realistic 2027 rotation candidate."

That timeline has grown murkier since. A lost 2025 season and an uneven return have turned Hampton's immediate value into a question of health and development, not imminent innings in the Bronx.

title: Kyle Lowry gets the Raptors honor only Vince Carter has received
description: Kyle Lowry’s legendary run with the Toronto Raptors is getting the ultimate recognition, as the franchise prepares to give the longtime point guard an honor only Vince Carter has received
fullText:
Kyle Lowry gets the Raptors honor only Vince Carter has received originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

Kyle Lowry helped deliver the greatest moment in Toronto Raptors history. Now, his place in the franchise's history will become permanent.

The Raptors announced Thursday that Lowry's No. 7 jersey will be retired following Toronto's Jan. 10 game against the Philadelphia 76ers at Scotiabank Arena. Lowry will become only the second player in franchise history to receive the honor, joining Vince Carter, whose No. 15 was raised to the rafters in November 2024.

The opponent adds another layer of significance to the celebration. Lowry is a Philadelphia native and spent the final two-plus seasons of his NBA career with the 76ers.

Lowry officially closed his 20-year career earlier this summer. The 40-year-old signed a ceremonial one-day contract with Toronto on July 7, allowing him to retire with the organization where he spent the most successful years of his career.

"I've been looking forward to this moment for years," Lowry said in a statement. "I always said that Toronto is home, and that I'd retire a Raptor, and to see my No. 7 go up in that building is going to mean everything to me."

Lowry's nine seasons in Toronto transformed him from a productive point guard into one of the most important players in franchise history.

He earned six consecutive All-Star selections as a Raptor and became a centerpiece of the team that captured the 2019 NBA championship, the first title in franchise history.

Lowry also established himself as one of the NBA's most productive guards during his lengthy career. He finished with averages of 13.8 points, 6.0 assists and 4.2 rebounds across 1,187 regular-season games.

His ability from beyond the arc also placed him among the league's most prolific shooters. Lowry retired with 2,209 made 3-pointers, ranking 14th in NBA history.

Lowry also played for the Memphis Grizzlies, Houston Rockets and Miami Heat before finishing his career in Philadelphia.

On Jan. 10, the Raptors will make sure No. 7 always remains part of it.

title: Colin Cowherd considered stand-up comedy
description: If you weren’t watching Colin Cowherd on TV and listening to him on the radio every day, maybe you would have been paying to see him perform as a comedian. Cowherd joined Shannon Spake on the Sons & Daughters podcast this week, where he discussed his upbringing and the path that led him to his career today. And…
fullText:
If you weren't watching Colin Cowherd on TV and listening to him on the radio every day, maybe you would have been paying to see him perform as a comedian.

Cowherd joined Shannon Spake on the Sons & Daughters podcast this week, where he discussed his upbringing and the path that led him to his career today. And during the podcast, Cowherd explained that he loves the process of building a show as much as he loves the show itself, crediting his preference for preparation over just flipping the mic on and improvising.

"Some days I like the process more than the show. So I've always trusted my business because I didn't just spitball. Even now I've got a staff and we're writing notes and notes and notes, my whole theory on broadcasting is you have to take the audience somewhere. Sometimes I'll listen to talk radio hosts, and they're just kind of making it up as they go. And my take is you got to respect the audience, and when somebody turns me on, I get 11 minutes until the commercial, I've got to make them laugh, make them think, make them something. You have to take people somewhere."

"Nobody's ever turned me off because I was wrong. They've turned me off when I'm boring," Cowherd continued, citing his own desire to seek interesting content when he was younger. "Most of the people I was drawn to were entertaining people. I would read the newspaper, but even newspaper people- the funnier the columnist, the more clever the columnist, the more I was drawn to it. So I just know what I was drawn to. It was always colorful, outspoken, funny people. They have an influence on you. I like an opinion, I like telling stories, I like making people laugh. At one point, I thought I would do stand-up comedy."

Cowherd was never the type of radio host to just rely on the box score or take call after call. And he certainly makes listeners think through his ability to draw analogies and his willingness to take opposing stances. But the comedy itch seemingly has not totally left Cowherd, with the longtime sports radio host previously helping CBS develop a sitcom that never aired. He's also named as an executive producer on a workplace romantic comedy for ABC starring Rob Lowe that is still listed as in development.

Even without his sitcom ventures, there is an aspect of comedy or scriptwriting to the way Cowherd builds his show, which relies on a staff of writers. Cowherd went on to cite Robin Williams' ability to make it look like he was ad-libbing while performing.

"He wasn't ad-libbing; he knew where he was going," Cowherd claimed. "I know where I'm going every segment. The audience doesn't know where I'm going; I know where I'm going. Because I think you have to take people places."

title: Patriots vs. Browns live updates: Score, news, discussion from NFL preseason
description: The Patriots will conclude their preseason Thursday night.
fullText:
For the first time this season the New England Patriots hit the road as they get set to conclude their preseason against the Cleveland Browns.

Drake Maye and the Patriots frontline players will not play again Thursday night, as the emphasis remains on health with Week 1 just under two weeks away. In total, 38 players are not in uniform which includes a handful of those already dealing with injuries.

Follow along live down below throughout preseason game No. 3.

Thursday, Aug. 27, 8 p.m. ET | Huntington Bank Field, Cleveland, OH | Broadcast information | Game day roster

The Patriots lost the coin toss putting the defense on the field first against Dillon Gabriel and the Browns reserves. A third-down defensive pass interference penalty downfield on Kindle Vildor quickly put Cleveland outside the red zone. From there, the Browns needed just four plays to find the end zone. [Patriots 0 : 7 Browns]

Tommy DeVito drew the start for the Patriots with QB coach Ashton Grant calling offensive plays. After quickly working across midfield, DeVito and Kyle Williams struck again as they connected on a 45-yard touchdown down the left sideline. [Patriots 7 : 7 Browns]

Tommy DeVito drops it in to Kyle Williams for 6️⃣

NEvsCLE on Prime Video
Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/agDyHm0clX

The Browns offense quickly got back to work. Rookie Gabe Jacas bit on a zone-read to allow Gabriel to pick up a third-down with his legs, before the left quarterback found a pair of chunk gains through the air over the middle — the second being a 14-yard touchdown. [Patriots 7 : 14 Browns]

New England then went three-and-out on their next possession as a third-down pass was slightly behind and dropped by Lan Larison out of the backfield. New punter Matt Haack then punted away.

Cleveland's first play of its new drive goes 52 yards on a deep connection to wide receiver Ben Patterson. Multiple Patriots defenders wrap up Gabriel behind the line of scrimmage on third down in the red zone for a registered sack before kicker Andrew Szmyt adds three to the Browns' column from 35 yards out. Looking for a response, Morton drove the Patriots offense into the red zone, where kicker Andy Borregales made a 26-yard field goal attempt midway through the frame. New England's quarterback scrambled for a gain of 14 before connecting for 19 more yards with Kyle Dixon, sitting in a zone coverage soft spot, to cross midfield on the drive. Starting its response series just past midfield in New England territory after outside linebacker Amari Gainer was flagged for roughing the passer, Gabriel found running back Ahmani Marshall in the flat, who shed a tackle to secure the score. Cornerback Charles Woods allowed two chunk conversions totaling 39 yards prior. [Patriots 10 : 27 Browns]

The Patriots, taking over with just over two minutes remaining until halftime, had Borregales drill a 33-yard field goal with seven seconds left on the clock. A defensive pass interference call that overturned a deep Morton interception set the Patriots up in Cleveland territory before the no-huddle tempo took effect. [Patriots 13 : 27 Browns]

title: Rutgers football legend joins Greg Schiano’s coaching staff
description: One of Rutgers football's greatest players joined Greg Schiano's coaching staff last year.
fullText:
One of the greatest players in Rutgers football history is now helping future generations of Scarlet Knights.

Adam Korsak, a Ray Guy Award-winning punter who holds the NCAA record for career punts (349) and career punting yards (15,318), joined head coach Greg Schiano's staff as a Quality Control/Player Development assistant during the tail end of the 2025 season, according to an employment contract obtained by NJ.com via an open public records request.

The hire — which became official on November 1, 2025 — has not been previously reported. Korsak's addition was never announced by the program and his name is not currently listed on the football program's staff directory.

The Australian, who starred at Rutgers for five seasons between 2018 and 2022, is signed through the 2027 season. He is set to make $120,000 during the 2026 season and $130,000 during the 2027 season.

In his first five months on the job, Korsak received two retention bonuses totaling $45,000 ($25,000 on December 1, $20,000 on March 15). He was also entitled to up to $9,166.67 in relocation reimbursement, per his contract.

title: Detroit Lions sign former Cowboys, Chiefs CB ahead of preseason finale
description: Ahead of its preseason finale, the Detroit Lions signed former Dallas Cowboys and Kansas City Chiefs cornerback Eric Scott Jr.
fullText:
Ahead of its preseason finale and then roster cuts, the Detroit Lions inked former Dallas Cowboys and Kansas City Chiefs cornerback Eric Scott Jr. to its 90-man roster. Scott is a 6-foot, 197-pound corner.

Scott was drafted by the Cowboys in the sixth round of the 2023 NFL Draft. While he's yet to make his NFL debut, Scott may get the chance to impress and put some tape together in the Lions' final preseason game on Saturday at the Indianapolis Colts.

Whether it's with Detroit or another NFL franchise, a strong showing on Saturday against the Colts would set Scott up to potentially make a 53-man roster or an NFL practice squad.

Lions have placed EDGE Payton Turner on Reserve/Injured and signed DB Eric Scott. pic.twitter.com/pq9Pzy4kKg

Inactive throughout his 2023 rookie year, Scott was waived by Dallas near the end of training camp, then claimed by Kansas City, where he joined the Chiefs' 2024 practice squad. Unfortunately for Scott, he suffered an injury that forced him to the injured reserve near the end of training camp and cost him the entire 2025 season with the Chiefs.

Scott made the Cowboys roster entering his rookie season, but he never saw the field and was declared inactive each game. In 2024, the Cowboys waived Scott near the end of training camp. The Chiefs claimed Scott off waivers and he ended up on Kansas City's practice squad in 2024.

Then, an undisclosed injury forced Scott to the Chiefs' injured reserve in 2025.

Scott began his college career at Illinois State, transferred to Butler Community College, and finished at Southern Mississippi. Scott totaled four interceptions and 11 passes defended while at Southern Mississippi.

In its corresponding move, the Lions placed EDGE Payton Turner on injured reserve, ending his 2026 season before it ever began.

title: Roman Anthony Drops Encouraging Hint After Big WooSox Performance
description: Roman Anthony collected two hits for Worcester before offering a promising update on his potential Red Sox return.
fullText:
Roman Anthony Drops Encouraging Hint After Big WooSox Performance originally appeared on NESN. 

Roman Anthony appears to be closing in on the return the Boston Red Sox have been waiting for. Anthony delivered another encouraging performance during his rehab assignment with Triple-A Worcester on Thursday night. The young outfielder recorded two hits, including an RBI double, in the WooSox's 7-1 victory over the Scranton/Wilkes-Barre RailRiders at Polar Park.

The theme of the night was "Deuces Wild," and Anthony clearly understood the assignment. He finished 2-for-4 with a double, one RBI and one run scored. Anthony singled and scored in the first inning before adding an RBI double during Worcester's four-run sixth.

With two outs, Anthony lined a pitch into the gap to score Tsung-Che Cheng and extend the WooSox lead. The extra-base hit was his first double of the rehab assignment and provided another positive sign that his timing and power are returning.

Anthony now is hitting .333 with a 1.052 OPS during his time with Worcester.

The numbers were encouraging, but Anthony's comments after the game might have been even more important for Red Sox fans.

"I'm getting close to where I want to be," Anthony told NESN's Bridgette Proulx during a postgame interview.

Roman Anthony with an RBI double, hit at 105 miles per hour pic.twitter.com/ZxCSQLRzrA

That certainly sounds like a player nearing the end of his rehab assignment, although Anthony stopped short of confirming his immediate plans.

According to Tommy Cassell, Anthony would not commit to traveling to New York on Friday to rejoin the Red Sox. The organization planned to reevaluate him after Thursday night's game before determining the next step.

That evaluation will carry considerable importance for Boston.

MORE: Red Sox Stars Take Important Step Before Crucial Yankees Series

Anthony's presence would give the Red Sox another impact bat as they continue their push late in the season. Thursday's performance showed he can make a difference in multiple ways. He reached base, scored a run and drove in another while showing the ability to hit the ball with authority.

The Red Sox do not need to rush one of their most important young players, especially if the club believes he needs another game or two to feel completely comfortable. Anthony's own assessment, however, suggests the finish line is approaching quickly.

His potential trip to New York remained uncertain when he left Polar Park on Thursday night. His progress did not.

Two hits, one double and one very encouraging quote made it another successful step toward Boston.

title: Tony Romo receives 3 new citations following OWI arrest in Milwaukee
description: Romo is due in court on Sept. 21. It's unclear if he'll call games for CBS Sports again.
fullText:
Tony Romo has received three new citations stemming from his arrest in Milwaukee on suspicion of operating a vehicle while intoxicated, according to the Milwaukee Journal-Sentinel.

According to online court records, the former Dallas Cowboys quarterback and current CBS Sports analyst was cited for first-offense operating while intoxicated, unsafe passing on the right side and possessing open intoxicants in his vehicle. Romo had already received a citation on July 27 for refusing to take an intoxication test after his arrest.

Romo is reportedly due in court for all four citations on Sept. 21.

His camp also released a new statement to the Journal-Sentinel:

"Tony accepts full responsibility for his actions and has taken proactive steps to ensure that this isolated civil matter is properly resolved. We are working with local authorities to bring this matter to a close and we are communicating with CBS about next steps."

Romo was arrested on July 23 after being pulled over on a Milwaukee highway and performing poorly on a field sobriety test, according to police.

In addition to legal repercussions, Romo was soon placed on indefinite leave by CBS Sports. His future with the network remains uncertain, with company president David Berson declining to provide a timetable for a final decision while speaking with reporters earlier this month.

Romo was once the darling of NFL media and CBS paid him like it with a record-shattering 10-year, $180 million contract in 2020. His luster had worn off considerably even before the arrest, with his meandering and casual commentary style wearing thin for many fans.

So it might not be a surprise if CBS uses the arrest to get out of that contract and cut Romo loose. The Athletic noted his contract contains a morals clause that could allow CBS to void the deal if he embarrasses the company.

In the meantime, CBS is set to open the season with J.J. Watt working opposite Jim Nantz in its No. 1 booth.

title: Giants may have to shut down Willy Adames for remainder of their lost season
description: The timeline for San Francisco Giants shortstop Willy Adames to come back from his strained left elbow will probably prevent him from returning to action before the end of the 2026 season.
fullText:
Willy Adames, who prides himself on playing every day, might not be in the San Francisco Giants' lineup the rest of the way.

San Francisco's shortstop was scheduled for a platelet-rich plasma injection Thursday evening for his left elbow strain, followed by rest. According to the Giants the estimated recovery time is three to four weeks. With a month left in the season, that makes Adames' return to action in 2026 iffy, especially with no minor-league teams in action at that point for a rehab assignment.

"I don't know how reasonable or realistic that is," manager Tony Vitello said of Adames potentially playing again this season. Adames missed just two games with the Giants last year and one with Milwaukee the year before that.

Considering Adames' season-long struggle with back issues, it might make even less sense to rush his return, and the Giants aren't contending. Getting a look at younger players is among the current priorities. While Vitello said that Adames could get some DH at-bats, he noted that other players need those at-bats - notably Rafael Devers and Bryce Eldridge. The good news is that it appears Adames will not need surgery, and it's his non-throwing arm.

"You hate to jump to conclusions, but for now that's been ruled out," Vitello said.

Adames saw orthopedist Dr. Keith Meister in Dallas for a second opinion. Catcher/utility man Jesús Rodríguez is scheduled to see Meister after a setback during his return from elbow neuritis. Starter Adrian Houser, also diagnosed with an elbow strain this week, could return this season; he's not throwing for a few days and will be reexamined.

Kennedy let go: Infielder Buddy Kennedy, batting .116 on the season in 49 plate appearances, was designated for assignment to make room for Eldridge to come off the bereavement list. Kennedy's numbers weren't where he or the team wanted them to be, but the Giants, who acquired him twice this year, think highly of the 27-year-old infielder.

"Buddy was kind of the inside man," Vitello said. "He was probably involved day-to-day more than anybody with the younger guys and I think was a huge help."

Vitello said that Kennedy, rather than being sour at the news, went and asked various coaches, including Ron Washington, for ways he can continue to get better.

There's more to San Francisco with the Chronicle.

title: Ego Blockchain
description: Ego Blockchain Implementation . Contribute to ego-blockchain/ego-blockchain- development by creating an account on GitHub.
fullText:
A post-quantum Layer-1 blockchain that pays node operators for contributing real infrastructure — storage, wireless coverage, retrieval and compute — rather than for burning electricity on proof-of-work.

Status: public testnet. The chain is live and producing blocks, but EGOC has no mainnet and is not tradeable. Mainnet launch follows an independent security audit. Testnet addresses use the egot prefix (chain_id = 1).

Ego is a single client that runs a full node and pays for measured contribution:

Stored files are split, encrypted with AES-256-GCM and distributed, so an operator never holds a complete file or knows its contents.

Every key is post-quantum from genesis — not a planned migration:

Requires Rust 1.85 or newer (the workspace uses edition 2024) and Node.js 20+ for the desktop app and SDK.

On Windows, link errors of the form LNK1318 are resolved by using rust-lld.exe rather than the MSVC linker.

See testnet/TESTNET.md for multi-node setup. Each node on the same machine needs its own EGO_DATA_DIR, or they will contend for the same RocksDB lock.

Maximum supply is 1,000,000,000 EGOC (1 EGOC = 1,000,000 uEGOC). Genesis allocations, defined in ego-desktop/src-tauri/src/tokenomics.rs:

Block emissions release at 0.0832 EGOC per block with a halving every ~4 years, targeting a 120-year schedule. Transaction fees split 60% to block producers and 40% to the staking pool. Foundation funds vest linearly over 48 months, enforced at block-write time rather than by policy.

A 10,000,000 EGOC faucet is minted on testnet only and is excluded from mainnet genesis.

Issues and pull requests are welcome. Consensus, cryptography and tokenomics changes are consensus-critical: please open an issue describing the problem before submitting a change to those areas.

title: Study captures how smog begins
description: Scientists have finally observed a fleeting chemical reaction that forms the basis of urban smog. The insight could help improve air quality forecasting models.
fullText:
Scientists have directly observed a fleeting chemical reaction that creates a key ingredient in urban smog. The research offers insight into the earliest stages of pollution formation and could help improve air quality forecasting models.

The researchers directly tracked short-lived molecules called Criegee intermediates as they formed when ozone reacted with isoprene, a gas released in large quantities by trees and other plants. These highly reactive molecules help drive atmospheric chemistry that can ultimately affect air pollution and particle formation, but scientists had previously understood them mainly through indirect evidence.

The study, published in Nature Communications, was performed by UC Riverside chemist and first author Lei Yang as well as corresponding author Jingsong Zhang, UCR chemistry professor, and several doctoral students.

Though unfamiliar to most people, isoprene is one of the most abundant chemicals released into the atmosphere. Trees and other plants emit hundreds of millions of tons of this gas every year, making natural vegetation one of the largest sources of reactive gases in the atmosphere.

Isoprene itself poses little direct harm. It belongs to a family of compounds called alkenes, which react with ozone in the atmosphere. When that happens, they launch a chain of chemical reactions that create particles called secondary organic aerosols that make up much of the haze hanging over cities, scatter sunlight, and can travel deep into the lungs.

Although trees produce most of the world’s isoprene, the findings do not suggest forests are driving air pollution. Instead, they highlight the importance of controlling ground-level ozone, which fuels these reactions.

“We can’t do anything about the alkenes or isoprene from trees,” Zhang said. “If you want to solve the air quality problem, you have to reduce ozone in the air. Ozone is the main driver. In practice, this means reducing emissions of its chemical precursors, especially nitrogen oxides and volatile organic compounds.”

Scientists have known for decades that ozone reacts with isoprene and other alkenes, but the first moments of that reaction have remained largely invisible. The chemistry unfolds in hundredths of a second, creating unstable molecules called Criegee intermediates that disappear almost as soon as they form. Despite being postulated 80 years ago by German organic chemist Rudolf Criegee, these intermediates are so short-lived they disappear before conventional techniques can detect them and have eluded direct observation or characterization in ozonolysis reactions.

“It’s like nature was presenting us with a dish, and we had to guess how it was made,” Zhang said. “Now we have a recipe.”

To capture these elusive molecules, the researchers used cavity ring-down spectroscopy, an ultrasensitive optical technique that passes light between mirrors roughly 10,000 times. Rather than collecting the molecules for analysis, the system observes them where they are created, allowing scientists to detect compounds that exist only briefly and in extremely low concentrations.

Using this approach, the team detected Criegee intermediates produced during isoprene’s reaction with ozone and tracked how they formed and disappeared over time. Those measurements allowed the researchers to determine reaction rates and test atmospheric reaction networks with direct observations instead of relying solely on the stable products left behind after the chemistry is complete.

The work builds on an earlier study, also published in Nature Communications, from Zhang’s laboratory that captured Criegee intermediates in simpler reactions involving smaller alkenes. Isoprene, with its more complex molecular structure and central role in atmospheric chemistry, presented a much greater challenge and carries broader environmental significance.

Better measurements of these early reactions could improve the atmospheric models scientists use to predict pollution events and understand how fine-particle pollution forms under different environmental conditions. While the study was conducted under controlled laboratory conditions, the researchers say it establishes a foundation for examining increasingly complex chemical reactions occurring in the real atmosphere.

Next, the team plans to apply the same techniques to pinenes, another major class of compounds emitted naturally by trees, to better understand how they react with ozone and contribute to air pollution.

“For eight decades, scientists could only infer what happened during the first instant of these reactions,” Zhang said. “Now we can watch them happen. That gives us the best picture yet of how ozone transforms natural emissions into the compounds that shape our atmosphere.”

description: Claude subscription wire compatibility for Pi. Contribute to paoloanzn/pi-black development by creating an account on GitHub.
fullText:
Use your Claude Max (or Pro) subscription with Pi.

Pi Black is an unofficial Pi package that routes Anthropic OAuth requests through your existing Claude subscription usage by applying Claude Code 2.1.224 request conventions. The existing source patch and standalone-binary build system remain available as a fallback.

Pi Black has three independently versioned compatibility surfaces:

The Pi package fails closed on versions other than 0.84.1, 0.84.2, and 0.84.3. Each new Pi version must be explicitly revalidated and added to the runtime allowlist; the package peer dependencies are "*" because Pi supplies its core packages at runtime.

Pi checks unpinned Git packages for updates in the background. When a newer Pi Black commit is available, Pi displays a package-update notice; apply it with:

For a reproducible install, pin a release tag:

Pinned packages do not move automatically. Install a newer tagged ref explicitly when you are ready to upgrade.

Then use Pi's normal Anthropic login:

The package replaces only the built-in Anthropic provider implementation and only transforms OAuth-token requests. It preserves Pi's credential storage, OAuth refresh, model behavior, tools, retries, streaming, and usage accounting. API-key requests and non-Anthropic providers pass through unchanged.

No identity environment variables are required. When Claude Code state exists, Pi Black reads the installation ID and account UUID from ~/.claude.json (or the location selected by CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR) in memory and adds matching request metadata. It does not copy, print, or persist those values.

Current subscription routing also works when that optional metadata is unavailable, as demonstrated by the standalone Pi Black binary with no identity variables in its environment.

For Anthropic OAuth requests, Pi Black reproduces the version-specific SDK-CLI request shape:

The checksum implementation validates and updates only the first billing system block. User content, tool results, descriptions, and nested model or max_tokens fields cannot redirect the placeholder patch.

Public CI uses fake transports only. It never makes provider requests and requires no credentials.

The Pi package is the recommended installation. macOS and Linux users who prefer the standalone patched build can install the latest native release as pi-black:

The installed launcher checks the latest release checksum at interactive startup. If the installed build differs, it offers to update before starting Pi Black. Downloads are checksum-verified; network-check failures are silent, while a rejected or failed update continues with the installed build. Set PI_BLACK_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1 to disable this check; Pi's PI_OFFLINE=1 also disables it.

Install a specific standalone release with PI_BLACK_RELEASE:

The repository pins an immutable commit from paoloanzn/pi, applies the patch under patches/, and delegates standalone compilation to Pi's release builder.

Build requirements and repeatability limits are in BUILD.md.

This project is unofficial and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Anthropic or the upstream Pi project. Users must provide their own valid account credentials and determine whether use complies with applicable service terms. The compatibility mechanism is version-specific and must be revalidated when Claude Code or Pi changes.

No OAuth tokens, identifiers, captures, or private Claude state are included in the package or release artifacts. Pi and the derived patch are distributed under the MIT license; see LICENSE.

title: Astronomers discover a new type of astrophysical object: A black hole star
description: Astronomers have discovered a “black hole star,” an extremely bright red spot in the early universe that appears to be a new type of astrophysical object. It resembles an enormous star, but its energy production is closer to what a black hole might generate.
fullText:
Astronomers at MIT and elsewhere have spotted an extremely bright red spot in the early universe. The object resembles an enormous star, spanning the size of our solar system. But it also is putting out 100 billion times more energy than any known star can physically produce. In fact, such energies are closer to what a black hole might generate.

The curious combination suggests that the red spot is an entirely new type of astrophysical source. The astronomers are calling it a “black hole star.”

In a paper appearing today in the journal Nature, the team presents their analysis of the new object, which they discovered using NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope (JWST). The telescope spotted the bright red dot in the very early universe, just a few hundred million years after the Big Bang.

The scientists conclude that the most likely explanation for the strange red dot is that it is a mashup of a black hole and a star — a combination that has never been observed until now. The object is likely a hugely dense cloud of gas, powered not by standard nuclear fusion, but by a central black hole.

“Our picture of this object is evolving very rapidly,” says lead author Rohan Naidu, a NASA Hubble Fellow and Pappalardo Fellow at MIT’s Kavli Institute for Astrophysics and Space Research (MKI). “We think there is a central black hole that is 100,000 times as massive as the sun. And around this black hole, there would be this very extended envelope of gas that looks like a star the size of the solar system. It’s huge.”

If the bright red dot is indeed a black hole star, it would help to solve the identity of other mysterious “little red dots” that have appeared in nearly every deep space image JWST has taken to date.

“These little red dots seem to be everywhere in the early universe but essentially disappear by the present day,” Naidu says. “What exactly these objects are has been one of the most debated topics of the JWST era.”

The study’s MIT co-authors are MKI Director Robert Simcoe, the Bruno B. Rossi Professor of Experimental Physics; and Wendy Sun ’26, along with collaborators from multiple other institutions.

Naidu and his colleagues didn’t intend to find a black hole star. They were looking for the most distant, earliest galaxies, as part of a survey that they named “Mirage or Miracle” (MoM). The team used the JWST to look into deep space, back when the universe was a few hundred million years old. Their goal was to look for galaxies that actually formed at those early times.

“There’s been this puzzle of many bright galaxies showing up at extremely early times,” Naidu says. “What we found was that what looks like an extremely bright early galaxy, aka a ‘miracle,’ in some cases actually could be a ‘mirage.’”

As they looked through JWST’s images for intriguing sources to target with their survey, they noticed a feature that stood out from the rest: a dot that was very red, and very bright.

“When we see something very red in the universe, we often assume that it is surrounded by dust, like soot or ash,” Simcoe explains. “The same way that the wildfire smoke from Canada recently made the sky in Boston look bright red, astronomical objects can also appear redder than their intrinsic color when you see them through a veil of dust.”

But there were other signatures in the light that didn’t quite match up with what physicists expect from dust. The team also observed another strange pattern: The dot’s light was extremely bright, except below certain wavelengths, where the light completely disappeared. 

This spectral drop-off is known as a “Balmer break” — a signature traditionally associated with dense gas soaking up photons in the atmospheres of stars that are a few hundred millions of years old. Vega, one of the brightest stars in the night sky shows exactly this pattern.

“The break we observed in this object is the deepest break we have ever observed in any object, ruling out ‘ordinary’ stars as the source,” Naidu says. “But it made us wonder if we were seeing a new kind of ‘stellar atmosphere,’ but on a spectacular scale.”

What’s more, the red dot’s light contained almost no signature of metals or any elements other than hydrogen and helium. “It was truly singular in so many ways,” Naidu says.

To puzzle out what the source of the red dot could be, the team ran simulations of different scenarios to see what combination of astrophysical features could produce the red dot’s distinctive color.

“We started to ask: Could you make something that red using just hydrogen, without any dust?” Simcoe says. “To our surprise, it turns out you can, if you have an extremely dense screen of hydrogen, so dense that it looks more like the surface of an enormous star than a wispy interstellar nebula.”

Their simulations pointed to the red dot possibly being some powerful enshrouded energy source, surrounded by an extremely dense cocoon of hydrogen. If this were the case, it would explain the light-blocking Balmer break and the lack of anything other than hydrogen and helium that the astronomers observed. But it still wouldn’t explain the object’s extreme brightness.

“You have something that looks a bit like a star but is 100 billion times brighter,” Naidu says. “That means you can’t be powering this by nuclear fusion, which is the energy source that sits at the heart of all the stars we have.”

Black holes, however, routinely produce energy at the scales the team observed. Naidu and his colleagues incorporated an active, accreting black hole into their simulations of the hydrogen-cocooned star and varied the black hole’s mass, along with other parameters. They then compared the resulting brightness of the simulated “black hole star” with the brightness that JWST observed from the red dot.

From these simulations, they found the closest match, and concluded that the most likely scenario to explain the red dot, is a black hole star. Specifically, the object likely contains a central black hole that is about 100,000 times as massive as the sun. This powerful core is surrounded by a dense, star-like cocoon of hydrogen that is roughly the size of the solar system.

The team has named the object MoM-BH*-1, after the survey that detected it, as well as the moniker “black hole star – one,” which implies that the object is the first of others. The researchers suspect that black hole stars could explain many of the other little red dots that appear in JWST images. Those objects are not as bright as MoM-BH*-1.

“Every little red dot is consistent with being a black hole star, embedded in a generic early galaxy,” Naidu says. “But what is special about MoM-BH*-1 is, the black hole star is essentially completely outshining its surrounding host galaxy, such that we’re seeing pure black hole star light.”

This research was supported, in part, by the MIT Department of Physics, NASA, and the Space Telescope Science Institute.
